title: حِكَايَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ
titleEn: The Jew's Tale ends; the Tailor's Tale begins: the Lame Young Man and the Barber
part: Night 29 · The Jew's Tale ends / The Tailor's Tale begins
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 232–239 (Night 29, continuing directly from nights-28), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 29 resumes the Jew's tale: the young man with the severed hand is freed by the lord (the governor's superior), who proves to be the father of the two sisters, and is married to the younger daughter; he ends by explaining why his right hand was cut off. The King of China, unmoved, says the hunchback's tale is more wondrous and threatens to hang them all; the tailor steps forward with his own tale. At a feast he describes, a lame young man from Baghdad refuses to sit with a barber and tells why: his love for the judge's daughter, the old go-between, and the talkative barber, whom he summoned on a Friday to shave his head. The night ends with the barber's astrological chatter, mid-tale. Verse is copied as printed. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some of the Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّاكَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammākānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿatu wa-al-ʿishrūna
sentences.l: So when it was the night, the ninth and the twenty
sentences.i: And when it was the twenty-ninth night,
sentences.n: The night formula. The print runs fa-lammā and kānat together as one word, and the tens take nominative -ūna as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهُ لَمَّا قَالَ لِلدَّلَّالِ اِقْبِضِ الْأَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahu lammā qāla li-al-dallāli iqbiḍi al-alfa dirhamin
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the fortunate, that he, when he said to the broker, “Seize the thousand dirham,”
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when he said to the broker, “Take the thousand dirhams,”
sentences.n: Shahrazād resumes. The youth is still the speaker, and the sentence runs on through the next unit, where its main verb arrives with ʿarafa.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الدَّلَّالُ ذَلِكَ عَرَفَ أَنَّ قَضِيَّتَهُ مُشْكِلَةٌ فَمَضَى بِالْعِقْدِ أِلَى كَبِيرِ السُّوقِ وَأَعْطَاهُ لَهُ فَأَخَذَ وَتَوَجَّهَ أِلَى الْوَالِى وَقَالَ لَهُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْعِقْدَ سُرِقَ مِنْ عِنْدِي وَوَجَدْنَا الْحَرَامِيَّ لَابِسٌ لُبْسَ أَوْلَادِ التُّجَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-dallālu dhālika ʿarafa anna qaḍiyyatahu mushkilatun fa-maḍā bi-al-ʿiqdi ilā kabīri al-sūqi wa-aʿṭāhu lahu fa-akhadha wa-tawajjaha ilā al-wālī wa-qāla lahu anna hādhā al-ʿiqda suriqa min ʿindī wa-wajadnā al-ḥarāmiyya lābisun lubsa awlādi al-tujjāri
sentences.l: So when the broker heard that, he knew that his case was problematic, and he went off with the necklace to the chief of the market and gave it to him, and he took and headed to the governor and said to him: “This necklace was stolen from me, and we found the thief wearing the dress of the sons of the merchants.”
sentences.i: When the broker heard that, he knew he was in an awkward position. So he took the necklace to the chief of the market and gave it to him, and the chief took it and went to the governor and said, “This necklace was stolen from me, and we have found the thief dressed in the clothes of merchants’ sons.”
sentences.n: The subject shifts at fa-akhadha: it is the chief of the market who takes the necklace to the governor and speaks, though the print gives no sign of the change. lābis is printed bare; we point it as a nominative, a loose circumstantial where Classical would write the accusative lābisan. al-ḥarāmī, 'the thief', is a colloquial word (from ḥarām, 'forbidden').

sentences.t: فَمَا أَشْعُرُ أِلَّا وَالظَّلَمَةُ أَحَاطُوابِي وَأَخَذُونِي وَوَدُّونِي لِلْوَالِى
sentences.tr: fa-mā ashʿuru illā wa-al-ẓalamatu aḥāṭūbī wa-akhadhūnī wa-waddūnī li-al-wālī
sentences.l: So I did not perceive, except and the oppressors had surrounded me and seized me and taken me to the governor.
sentences.i: Before I knew it, the guards had surrounded me, seized me and led me off to the governor.
sentences.n: fa-mā ashʿuru illā wa-… is a stock turn, 'I was aware of nothing until'. al-ẓalama, 'the oppressors', is the common word for the governor's men. waddūnī is a Middle Arabic 'they conveyed me', from wadda for Classical waddā; the final alif of aḥāṭūbī is the plural alif, printed run together with the next word.

sentences.t: فَسَأَلَنِي الْوَالِى عَنْ ذَلِكَ الْعِقْدِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مَا قُلْتُهُ لِلدَّلَّالِ
sentences.tr: fa-saʾalanī al-wālī ʿan dhālika al-ʿiqdi fa-qultu lahu mā qultuhu li-al-dallāli
sentences.l: Then the governor asked me about that necklace, and I said to him what I had said to the broker.
sentences.i: The governor questioned me about the necklace, and I told him what I had told the broker.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الْوَالِى وَقَالَ مَاهَذَا كَلَامُ الْحَقِّ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-wālī wa-qāla māhādhā kalāmu al-ḥaqqi
sentences.l: Then the governor laughed and said: This is-not the speech of the truth.
sentences.i: The governor laughed and said, “That is not truthful talk.”
sentences.n: mā and hādhā are printed as one word. We read mā as a negative; it could also be 'what is this? Is it the speech of truth?'

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَدْرِ أِلَّا وَأَنَا تَعَرَّيْتُ مِنْ ثِيَابِي وَضُرِبْتُ بِالْمَقَارِعِ عَلَى أَجْنَابِي فَحَرَقَنِي الضَّرْبُ فَقُلْتُ أَنَا سَرَقْتُهُ وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي أَلَا حَسَنٌ أَنَّكَ تَقُولُ أَنَا سَرَقْتُهُ وَلَا أَقُولُ أَنَّ صَاحِبَتَهُ مَقْتُولَةٌ عِنْدِي فَيَقْتُلُونِي فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lam adri illā wa-anā taʿarraytu min thiyābī wa-ḍuribtu bi-al-maqāriʿi ʿalā ajnābī fa-ḥaraqanī al-ḍarbu fa-qultu anā saraqtuhu wa-qultu fī nafsī alā ḥasanun annaka taqūlu anā saraqtuhu wa-lā aqūlu anna ṣāḥibatahu maqtūlatun ʿindī fa-yaqtulūnī fīhā
sentences.l: Then I did not know, except and I was stripped of my clothes and was beaten with the rods upon my sides, and the beating burned me, so I said, “I stole it.” And I said in myself: Is-it-not good that you say, “I stole it,” and do not say that its owner is killed at my place, so that they kill me on her account?
sentences.i: Before I knew it, I was stripped of my clothes and beaten with rods across my sides, and the beating seared me, so I said, “I stole it.” And I told myself, “Better that you say ‘I stole it’ than say that its owner lies murdered in my keeping, so that they kill me for her.”
sentences.n: The print has ālā ḥasan as two words; it may be the printer's break for al-aḥsan, 'the best thing', but we point it as printed. -hu in ṣāḥibatahu most naturally refers to the necklace, 'its mistress'. fa-yaqtulūnī keeps the indicative where Classical would have the subjunctive after fa.

sentences.t: فَكَتَبُوا أَنِّي سَرَقْتُهُ فَقَطَعُوا يَدِي وَقَلَوْهَا فِى الزَّيْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-katabū annī saraqtuhu fa-qaṭaʿū yadī wa-qalawhā fī al-zayti
sentences.l: Then they wrote that I had stolen it, and they cut my hand and fried it in the oil.
sentences.i: So they recorded that I had stolen it, cut off my hand and seared it in oil.
sentences.n: Searing the stump in hot oil was the way of stopping the bleeding.

sentences.t: فَغُشِيَ عَلَيَّ فَسَقَوْنِي الشَّرَابَ حَتَّى أَفَقْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-ghushiya ʿalayya fa-saqawnī al-sharāba ḥattā afaqtu
sentences.l: Then it was covered upon me, and they gave me the drink to drink until I came to.
sentences.i: I fainted, and they gave me a draught to drink until I came to.
sentences.n: ghushiya ʿalayya, literally 'it was covered over me', is the idiom for fainting.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُ يَدِي وَجِئْتُ أِلَى الْقَاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtu yadī wa-jiʾtu ilā al-qāʿati
sentences.l: Then I took my hand and came to the hall.
sentences.i: Then I took up my severed hand and went back to my lodging.
sentences.n: al-qāʿa, 'the hall', is the room in which the narrator lodges. Its owner, ṣāḥib al-qāʿa, is his landlord.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ صَاحِبُ الْقَاعَةِ حَيْثُ مَاجَرَي لَكَ هَذَا خَلِّ الْقَاعَةَ وَانْظُرْلَكَ مَوْضِعًا آخَرَ لِأَنَّكَ مُتَّهَمٌ بِالْحَرَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ṣāḥibu al-qāʿati ḥaythu mājarā laka hādhā khalli al-qāʿata wa-unẓurlaka mawḍiʿan ākhara li-annaka muttahamun bi-al-ḥarāmi
sentences.l: Then the owner of the hall said: Since what-happened to you, this, leave the hall and look-for-yourself another place, because you are accused of the forbidden.
sentences.i: Then the landlord said, “Since this has befallen you, leave the room and find yourself another place, for you are under suspicion of theft.”
sentences.n: ḥaythu is used causally, 'since'. mā and jarā are printed run together, the final letter a yā as printed. bi-al-ḥarām, 'of the forbidden', means here of theft.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ سَيِّدِي اصْبِرْ عَلَيَّ يَوْمَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَٰثَةً حَتَّى أَنْظُرَأَيَّ مَوْضِعًا قَٰلَ نَعَمْ وَمَضَى وَتَرَكَنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu sayyidī iṣbir ʿalayya yawmayni aw thalāthatan ḥattā anẓura ayya mawḍiʿan qāla naʿam wa-maḍā wa-tarakanī
sentences.l: So I said to him: My lord, be-patient upon me two days or three, until I look [at] any place. He said: Yes, and went off and left me.
sentences.i: I said to him, “My lord, bear with me for two or three days, until I find a place.” He said, “Very well,” and went away and left me.
sentences.n: anẓurāy is one printed word, which we read as anẓura ayya, 'until I look at some place'. It may be garbled for anẓura lī, 'until I look out for myself' (compare the landlord's unẓur laka just above); the form is obscure. thalātha and qāla are printed defectively (ثلثة, قل) and pointed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَبَقِيتُ قَاعِدًا أَبْكِي وَأَقُولُ كَيْفَ أَرْجِعُ أِلَى أَهْلِي وَأَنَا مَقْطُوعُ الْيَدِ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنِّي بَرِيٌّ فَلَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَمْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-baqītu qāʿidan abkī wa-aqūlu kayfa arjiʿu ilā ahlī wa-anā maqṭūʿu al-yadi wa-lam yaʿlamū annī barīyun fa-laʿalla Allāha yuḥdithu baʿda dhālika amran
sentences.l: So I remained sitting, I weep and I say: How do I return to my family, and I cut-off of the hand, and they did not know that I am innocent? So perhaps God brings-about after that a matter.
sentences.i: So I stayed there sitting, weeping and saying, “How can I go back to my family with my hand cut off, when they do not know that I am innocent? Perhaps God will bring something about after this.”
sentences.n: maqṭūʿu al-yadi, 'cut-off of the hand', is a passive participle governing its noun in an idafa; wa-anā … is a circumstantial clause. barī is printed without a hamza (Classical barīʾ).

sentences.t: وَبَكَيْتُ بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا فَلَمَّا مَضَى صَاحِبُ الْقَاعَةِ عَنِّي لَحِقَنِي غَمٌّ شَدِيدٌ فَتَشَوَّشْتُ يَوْمَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-bakaytu bukāʾan shadīdan fa-lammā maḍā ṣāḥibu al-qāʿati ʿannī laḥiqanī ghammun shadīdun fa-tashawwashtu yawmayni
sentences.l: And I wept a weeping severe. Then when the owner of the hall went away from me, a severe grief overtook me, and I was distraught two days.
sentences.i: I wept bitterly. After the landlord left me, heavy grief overtook me, and for two days I was beside myself.

sentences.t: وَفِي الْيَوْمِ الثَّالِثِ مَا أَدْرِي أِلَّا وَصَاحِبُ الْقَاعَةِ جَاءَنِي وَمَعَهُ بَعْضُ الظَّلَمَةِ وَكَبِيرُ السُّوقِ فَادَّعَى أَنِّي سَرَقْتُ الْعِقْدَ
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-yawmi al-thālithi mā adrī illā wa-ṣāḥibu al-qāʿati jāʾanī wa-maʿahu baʿḍu al-ẓalamati wa-kabīru al-sūqi fa-iddaʿā annī saraqtu al-ʿiqda
sentences.l: And on the day the third, I did not know, except and the owner of the hall came to me, and with him some of the oppressors and the chief of the market, and he claimed that I had stolen the necklace.
sentences.i: On the third day, before I knew it, the landlord came to me with some of the guards and the chief of the market, and one of them claimed that I had stolen the necklace.
sentences.n: The subject of fa-iddaʿā is not marked; it may be the landlord or the chief of the market. The turn mā adrī illā wa-… repeats the earlier 'I knew nothing until'.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجْتُ لَهُمْ وَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ مَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajtu lahum wa-qultu lahum mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: So I went out to them and said to them: What the news?
sentences.i: I went out to them and said, “What is the matter?”

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يُمْهِلُونِي دُونَ أَنْ كَتَّفُونِي وَرَمَوْافِي رَقَبَتِي جَنْزِيرًا وَقَالُوا لِي الْعِقْدُ الَّذِي كَانَ مَعَكَ طَلَعَ لِصَاحِبِ دِمَشْقَ وَوَزِيرِهَا وَحَاكِمِهَا وَقَالُوا أَنَّ هَذَا الْعِقْدَ عَدِمَ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ مِنْ مُدَّةِ ثَلَٰثِ سِنِينَ مَعَ ابْنَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yumhilūnī dūna an kattafūnī wa-ramawāfī raqabatī janzīran wa-qālū lī al-ʿiqdu alladhī kāna maʿaka ṭalaʿa li-ṣāḥibi Dimashqa wa-wazīrihā wa-ḥākimihā wa-qālū anna hādhā al-ʿiqda ʿadima min ʿindihi min muddati thalāthi sinīna maʿa ibnatihi
sentences.l: Then they did not give-me-respite without that they bound me and cast around my neck a chain, and they said to me: The necklace that was with you has come-out for the master of Damascus, and its vizier and its ruler. And they said: This necklace was lost from his possession from a period of three years, with his daughter.
sentences.i: They gave me no respite but bound me and hung a chain about my neck, and they said to me, “The necklace that was with you turns out to belong to the lord of Damascus, its vizier and its governor.” And they said, “This necklace went missing from him three years ago, together with his daughter.”
sentences.n: dūna an means 'before, until' here. ramawāfī is printed as one word, the plural alif run together with fī. wa-wazīrihā wa-ḥākimihā stand in apposition to ṣāḥib Dimashq: the lord of the city is its vizier and ruler. ʿadima, 'was lost', is the text's verb where Classical would say fuqida.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ مِنْهُمْ غَطَسَ قَلْبِي وَقُلْتُ رَاحَتْ رُوحُكَ لَامَحَالَةَ وَاللَّهِ لَابُدَّ أَنْ أَحْكِىَ لِلصَّاحِبِ حِكَايَتِي فَأِنْ شَاءَ قَتَلَنِي وَأِنْ شَاءَ عَفَا عَنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu hādhā al-kalāma minhum ghaṭasa qalbī wa-qultu rāḥat rūḥuka lāmaḥālata wa-llāhi lābudda an aḥkiya li-al-ṣāḥibi ḥikāyatī fa-in shāʾa qatalanī wa-in shāʾa ʿafā ʿannī
sentences.l: So when I heard this speech from them, my heart dived, and I said: Your soul has gone, without-escape! And by God, no-escape that I tell the master my story; so if he wills he kills me, and if he wills he pardons me.
sentences.i: When I heard these words from them, my heart sank, and I said to myself, “Your life is surely gone. By God, I must tell the lord my story: if he wishes, he will kill me, and if he wishes, he will pardon me.”
sentences.n: lāmaḥāla and lābudda are each printed as one word. In the conditionals the Arabic uses the perfect, shāʾa qatalanī, 'if he wills, he kills me', for a future sense.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلْنَا لِلصَّاحِبِ أَوْقَفَنِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣalnā li-al-ṣāḥibi awqafanī bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: So when we arrived at the master, he made me stand between his two hands.
sentences.i: When we reached the lord, he made me stand before him.
sentences.n: bayna yadayhi, 'between his two hands', means 'in his presence'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي نَظَرَ أِلَيَّ بِطَرْفِ عَيْنِهِ وَقَالَ لِلْحَاضِرِينَ لِمَ قَطَعْتُمْ يَدَهُ لِأَنَّ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ مِسْكِينٌ وَلَيْسَ لَهُ ذَنْبٌ وَقَدْ ظَلَمْتُمُوهُ بِقَطْعِكُمْ يَدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī naẓara ilayya bi-ṭarfi ʿaynihi wa-qāla li-al-ḥāḍirīna lima qaṭaʿtum yadahu li-anna hādhā al-rajula miskīnun wa-laysa lahu dhanbun wa-qad ẓalamtumūhu bi-qaṭʿikum yadahu
sentences.l: So when he saw me, he looked at me with the corner of his eye and said to those-present: Why did you cut his hand? Because this man is wretched and has no fault, and you have wronged him by your cutting of his hand.
sentences.i: When he saw me, he looked at me out of the corner of his eye and said to those present, “Why did you cut off his hand? This man is a poor wretch with no guilt, and you have wronged him by cutting off his hand.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ قَوِيَ قَلْبِى وَطَابَتْ نَفْسِي وَقُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ يَاسَيِّدِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu hādhā al-kalāma qawiya qalbī wa-ṭābat nafsī wa-qultu wa-llāhi yāsayyidī
sentences.l: So when I heard this speech, my heart grew strong and my self became good, and I said: By God, O my lord,
sentences.i: When I heard these words, my heart took courage and my spirit was eased, and I said, “By God, my lord,”
sentences.n: The sentence is cut here at the edge of the slice; the speech continues in the next unit. yā and sayyidī are printed as one word.

sentences.t: لَسْتُ بِسَارِقٍ وَقَدِ اتَّهَمُونِى بِهَذِهِ التُّهْمَةِ الْعَظِيمَةِ وَضَرَبُونِي بِالْمَقَارِعِ فِي بَطْنِ السُّوقِ وَحَكَمُوا عَلَيَّ بِأَنْ أُقِرَّ فَكَذَبْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِى وَاعْتَرَفْتُ بِالسَّرِقَةِ وَأَنَا بَرِيِّى مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: lastu bi-sāriqin wa-qadi ittahamūnī bi-hādhihi al-tuhmati al-ʿaẓīmati wa-ḍarabūnī bi-al-maqāriʿi fī baṭni al-sūqi wa-ḥakamū ʿalayya bi-an uqirra fa-kadhabtu ʿalā nafsī wa-iʿtaraftu bi-al-sariqati wa-anā barīyyī minhā
sentences.l: I am-not a thief, and they accused me of this great accusation, and beat me with the whips in the belly of the market, and ruled against me that I confess; so I lied against myself, and confessed to the theft, while I was innocent of it,
sentences.i: I am no thief, yet they accused me of this grave charge, beat me with rods in the middle of the market, and ruled that I must confess; so I lied against myself and confessed to the theft, though I was innocent of it,
sentences.n: The sentence began before this section: the youth is telling the lord his story, and the verb that governs 'I am not a thief' lies just outside our view. The print gives بريى, which looks like barīʾ, 'innocent', spelled with an extra yāʾ; the pointing barīyyī is a best guess at that form. maqāriʿ are whips or rods; 'the belly of the market' is the middle of it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الصَّاحِبُ لَابَأْسَ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ṣāḥibu lā-baʾsa ʿalayka
sentences.l: So the lord said, 'No harm upon you.'
sentences.i: The lord said, 'Fear nothing.'
sentences.n: al-ṣāḥib, literally 'the companion', is the title this story gives the great man; he plainly holds office, since he can command the chief of the market. lā baʾsa ʿalayka is the stock phrase of reassurance. The print runs lā and baʾs together as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَسَمَ عَلَى كَبِيرَالسُّوقِ وَقَٰلَ لَهُ أَعْطِ لِهَذَا دِيَةَ يَدِهِ وَإِلَّا أَشْنُقُكَ وَآخُذُ جَمِيعَ مَالَكَ
sentences.tr: thumma rasama ʿalā kabīra-al-sūqi wa-qāla lahu aʿṭi li-hādhā diyata yadihi wa-illā ashnuquka wa-ākhudhu jamīʿa mālika
sentences.l: Then he decreed upon the chief-of-the-market, and said to him, 'Give to this one the blood-price of his hand, and if-not I hang you and take all your property.'
sentences.i: Then he gave orders to the chief of the market, and said to him, 'Pay this man the price of his hand, or else I will hang you and seize everything you own.'
sentences.n: The print has قل for قال, so it is pointed with a dagger alif (qāla); the letters stay as printed. kabīr al-sūq is likewise printed as one word. rasama ʿalā means 'to give orders to'. diyat yadihi is the compensation owed for the youth's hand.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَاحَ عَلَى الْمُقَدَّمِينَ فَأَخَذُوهُ وَجَرُّوهُ وَبَقِيتُ أَنَا وَالصَّاحِبُ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣāḥa ʿalā al-muqaddamīna fa-akhadhūhu wa-jarrūhu wa-baqītu anā wa-al-ṣāḥibu
sentences.l: Then he cried upon the foremen, so they seized him and dragged him, and I remained, I and the lord,
sentences.i: Then he called to the officers, who seized the chief and dragged him away, and I was left alone with the lord;
sentences.n: al-muqaddamīn are the 'put-forward' ones, the headmen or officers of the watch. The man seized is the chief of the market, the object of the order just given.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ شَالُوا الْجِنْزِيرَ مِنْ عُنُقِي بِإِذْنِهِ وَحَلُّوا كِتَافِى فَنَظَرَ الصَّاحِبُ إِلَيَّ وَقَالَ يَا وَلَدِي اصْدُقْنِي وَحَدِّثْنِي كَيْفَ وَصَلَ إِلَيْكَ هَذَا الْعِقْدُ
sentences.tr: thumma shālū al-jinzīra min ʿunuqī bi-idhnihi wa-ḥallū kitāfī fa-naẓara al-ṣāḥibu ilayya wa-qāla yā waladī uṣduqnī wa-ḥaddithnī kayfa waṣala ilayka hādhā al-ʿiqdu
sentences.l: Then they lifted the chain from my neck by his permission, and loosed my bonds. And the lord looked at me and said, 'O my son, be-true-to-me and relate to me how this necklace reached you.'
sentences.i: Then, by his leave, they took the chain from my neck and loosed my bonds. The lord looked at me and said, 'My son, be truthful with me, and tell me how this necklace came to you.'
sentences.n: shālū, 'they lifted off', is the everyday verb for removing a load; kitāf are bonds or cords for tying. uṣduqnī takes the person as a direct object, 'be true to me'.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ ش—
sentences.tr: wa-qāla sh—
sentences.l: And he said, sh—
sentences.i: And he said:
sentences.n: The print breaks off here in a dash after shīn, so the word is cut. The verse that follows suggests it was shiʿr, 'verse', the very word that introduces the next poem.

sentences.t: عَلَيْكَ بِالصِّــدْقِ وَلَوْ اَنَّهُ * اَحْرَقَكَ الصِّدْقُ بِنَارِ الْوَعِيـــدِ
sentences.tr: ʿalayka bi-al-ṣidqi wa-law annahu * aḥraqaka al-ṣidqu bi-nāri al-waʿīdi
sentences.l: Upon you, truthfulness, even if that-it burned you, the truth, with the fire of the threat.
sentences.i: Hold fast to truth, even if truth should scorch you with the fire of threat.
sentences.n: Verse is printed with its own vowel marks and is kept exactly as printed. ʿalayka bi- followed by a noun is the idiom of exhortation, 'hold to ...'. In annahu and aḥraqaka the edition prints a bare alif with a fatḥa, not a hamza. The long strokes in al-ṣidq and al-waʿīd are only line-justification.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ يَا مَوْلَايَ أَقُولُ لَكَ الْحَقَّ ثُمَّ حَدَّثْتُهُ عَلَى مَاجَرَى لِي مَعَ الصَّبِيَّةِ الْأُولَى وَكَيْفَ جَاءَ تْنِي بِالثَّانِيَةِ وَكَيْفَ ذَبَحْتُهَا مِنَ الْغَيْرَةِ وَذَكَرْتُ لَهُ الْحَدِيثَ بِتَمَامِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu yā mawlāya aqūlu laka al-ḥaqqa thumma ḥaddathtuhu ʿalā mā-jarā lī maʿa al-ṣabiyyati al-ūlā wa-kayfa jāʾa tnī bi-al-thāniyati wa-kayfa dhabaḥtuhā mina al-ghayrati wa-dhakartu lahu al-ḥadītha bi-tamāmihi
sentences.l: So I said, 'O my lord, I say to you the truth.' Then I related to him what-had-happened to me with the first girl, and how she-came me with the second, and how I slaughtered her out-of the jealousy, and I mentioned to him the story in its completeness,
sentences.i: I said, 'My lord, I will tell you the truth.' Then I told him all that had passed between me and the first girl, and how she had brought me the second, and how I had slaughtered her in my jealousy; I recounted the whole story to him from beginning to end,
sentences.n: The print splits jāʾat-nī into two words, jāʾa tnī, 'she came to me'. jāʾa bi- is 'to come with', that is, 'to bring', so the girl who 'came with the second' is the elder, who brought her sister. ḥaddatha ʿalā has ʿalā where Classical would use ʿan or a direct object.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ كَلَامِي هَزَّ رَأْسَهُ وَضَرَبَ يَدَهُ الْيُمْنَى عَلَى الْيُسْرَى وَحَطَّ مِنْدِيلَهُ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ وَبَكَى سَاعَةً وَأَنْشَاءَ يَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa kalāmī hazza raʾsahu wa-ḍaraba yadahu al-yumnā ʿalā al-yusrā wa-ḥaṭṭa mindīlahu ʿalā wajhihi wa-bakā sāʿatan wa-anshāʾa yaqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: So when he heard my speech, he shook his head, and struck his hand the-right upon the left, and put his kerchief upon his face, and wept an hour; and he began to say verse:
sentences.i: When he heard my words he shook his head, struck his right hand upon his left, laid his kerchief over his face and wept for a time; then he began to recite:
sentences.n: wa-anshāʾa is the print's spelling of wa-anshaʾa, 'and he began', with an alif written before the final hamza; anshaʾa yaqūlu is 'he began to say'. raʾs is printed without its hamza. shiʿr, 'verse', stands bare as a label for the poem that follows.

sentences.t:
آرِي عِلَلَ الدُّنْيَا عَلَيَّ كَثِيــرَةً * وَصَاحِبُهَا حَتَّى الْمَمَاتِ عَلِيــلُ
لِكُلِّ اجْتِمَاعٍ مِنْ خَلِيلَيْنِ فُرْقَةٌ * وَكُلُّ الَّذِي دُونَ الْفِرَاقِ قَلِيلُ
sentences.tr:
ārī ʿilala al-dunyā ʿalayya kathīratan * wa-ṣāḥibuhā ḥattā al-mamāti ʿalīlu
li-kulli ijtimāʿin min khalīlayni furqatun * wa-kullu alladhī dūna al-firāqi qalīlu
sentences.l:
I-see the ailments of-the-world against me many, * and its companion, until death, is ailing.
For every meeting of two friends a parting, * and all that is short-of the separation is little.
sentences.i:
I see that the world's ills weigh heavily upon me, * and he who keeps its company is sick until death.
Every meeting of two friends ends in parting, * and whatever falls short of separation is slight.
sentences.n: Verse, kept exactly as printed. The first word is printed آرِي with madda and kasra; the sense and the metre want arā, 'I see', and the pointing is left as the edition has it. The strokes in kathīra and ʿalīl are line-justification. The last line means that every other grief is small beside parting.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيَّ وَقَالَ اعْلَمْ يَا وَلَدِى أَنَّ الصَّبِيَّةَ الْكَبِيرَةَ بِنْتِي وَكُنْتُ أَحْجُرُ عَلَيْهَا حَجْرًا عَظِيمًا فَلَمَّا بَلَغَتْ أَرْسَلْتُهَا مِصْرَ وَتَزَوَّجَتْ لِوَلَدِ عَمِّهَا فَمَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbala ʿalayya wa-qāla iʿlam yā waladī anna al-ṣabiyyata al-kabīrata bintī wa-kuntu aḥjuru ʿalayhā ḥajran ʿaẓīman fa-lammā balaghat arsaltuhā miṣra wa-tazawwajat li-waladi ʿammihā fa-māta
sentences.l: Then he turned to me and said, 'Know, O my son, that the girl the-elder is my daughter, and I used to confine her a great confinement; so when she came-of-age I sent her to Miṣr, and she married to the son of her uncle, and he died,
sentences.i: Then he turned to me and said, 'Know, my son, that the elder girl is my daughter. I kept her under strict guard, and when she came of age I sent her to Egypt, where she married her cousin, who then died;
sentences.n: The lord's speech begins here and runs on, unclosed, through the following units until the youth answers. Miṣr is Egypt, or Cairo, which the name also means. tazawwajat li- puts a lām before the husband where Classical would use a direct object. walad ʿammihā, 'the son of her paternal uncle', is her cousin.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ تْنِي وَقَدْ تَعَلَّمَتِ الْقُبْحَ مِنْ أَوْلَادِ مِصْرَ وَجَاءَتْكَ أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ ثُمَّ جَاءَتْكَ بِأُخْتِهَا الصَّغِيرَةِ وَالِاثْنَانِ شَقِيقَتَانِ وَكَانَتَا تُحِبَّانِ لِبَعْضِهِمَا بَعْضًا
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa tnī wa-qad taʿallamati al-qubḥa min awlādi miṣra wa-jāʾatka arbaʿa marrātin thumma jāʾatka bi-ukhtihā al-ṣaghīrati wa-al-ithnāni shaqīqatāni wa-kānatā tuḥibbāni li-baʿḍihimā baʿḍan
sentences.l: 'So she-came me, having learned the ugliness from the sons-of Miṣr, and she came to you four times; then she came to you with her sister the small-one; and the two were full-sisters, and the-two-of-them loved, for the-one-of-the-two, the-other.
sentences.i: 'She came back to me, having learned vile ways from the people of Egypt, and she came to you four times. Then she came to you with her younger sister. The two were full sisters and loved one another.
sentences.n: Again the print splits jāʾat-nī as jāʾa tnī. qubḥ, 'ugliness', is moral here: depravity. awlād miṣr, 'sons of Miṣr', means the people of Egypt. li-baʿḍihimā baʿḍan is a loose reciprocal, 'each other'; Classical would say aḥaduhumā al-ākhar.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَرَى لِلْكَبِيرَةِ مَاجَرَى أَخْرَجَتْ سِرَّهَا عَلَى أُخْتِهَا فَطَلَبَتِ الذَّهَابَ مَعَهَا ثُمَّ رَجَعَتْ وَحْدَهَا فَسَأَلْتُهَا عَنْهَا فَوَجَدْ تُهَا تَبْكِي عَلَيْهَا وَقَالَتْ لِأُمِّهَا سِرًّا بِحَضْرَتِي عَلَى مَاجَرَى مِنْ ذَبْحِهَا لِأُخْتِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jarā li-al-kabīrati mā-jarā akhrajat sirrahā ʿalā ukhtihā fa-ṭalabati al-dhahāba maʿahā thumma rajaʿat waḥdahā fa-saʾaltuhā ʿanhā fa-wajad tuhā tabkī ʿalayhā wa-qālat li-ummihā sirran bi-ḥaḍratī ʿalā mā-jarā min dhabḥihā li-ukhtihā
sentences.l: 'So when what-had-happened happened to the elder, she revealed her secret to her sister, and she asked to-go with her; then she returned alone, so I asked her about her, and I found her weeping over her, and she said to her mother, secretly, in my presence, about what-had-happened, from the slaughtering of her, to her sister,
sentences.i: 'When what had happened to the elder had happened, she disclosed her secret to her sister and asked to go with her. Then she came back alone, and when I asked her about the other, I found her weeping for her. She told her mother, privately but in my presence, all that had passed: the slaughter of her sister,
sentences.n: fa-wajad tuhā is printed as two words, 'so I found her'. The last phrase is loosely built: min dhabḥihā li-ukhtihā is literally 'from her slaughter, to her sister', and the sense taken here is 'the slaughter of her sister'. The pronouns in this passage shift between the two girls and can be read more than one way.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ تَزَلْ تَبْكِي وَتَقُولُ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَزَالُ أَبْكِي عَلَيْهَا حَتَّى أَمُوتَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam tazal tabkī wa-taqūlu wa-al-llāhi lā azālu abkī ʿalayhā ḥattā amūta
sentences.l: 'and she did not cease weeping and saying, "By God, I shall-not cease weeping over her until I die."
sentences.i: 'and she never ceased to weep, and would say, "By God, I shall weep for her until I die."
sentences.n: lam tazal tabkī is 'she did not cease weeping'; lā azālu abkī, 'I shall not cease weeping', is the same idiom in the first person.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْأَمْرُ كَذَلِكَ فَانْظُرْ يَا وَلَدِي مَا جَرَى
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-amru kadhālika fa-unẓur yā waladī mā jarā
sentences.l: 'And the matter was like-that; so look, O my son, at what happened,
sentences.i: 'And so it was. Consider, my son, all that has happened,

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَشْتَهِي مِنْكَ أَنْ لَا تُخَالِفَنِي فِيمَا أَقُولُهُ لَكَ وَهُوَ أَنِّي أُزَوِّجُكَ ابْنَتِى الصَّغِيرَةَ فَإِنَّهَا لَيْسَتْ شَقِيقَةً لَهُمَا وَهِيَ بِكْرٌ وَلَمْ آخُذْ مِنْكَ مَهْرًا وَأَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا رَاتِبًا مِنْ عِنْدِي وَتَبْقَى عِنْدِي بِمَنْزِلَةِ وَلَدِي
sentences.tr: wa-anā ashtahī minka an lā tukhālifanī fīmā aqūluhu laka wa-huwa annī uzawwijuka ibnatī al-ṣaghīrata fa-innahā laysat shaqīqatan lahumā wa-hiya bikrun wa-lam ākhudh minka mahran wa-ajʿalu lakumā rātiban min ʿindī wa-tabqā ʿindī bi-manzilati waladī
sentences.l: and I desire from you that you not oppose me in what I say to you, and it is that I marry-you-off to my daughter the-small, for she is-not a full-sister to the-two-of-them, and she is a virgin, and I will-not take from you a dower, and I will-set for you-two an allowance from with-me, and you will-remain with me in the standing of my son.'
sentences.i: and I ask of you that you not go against me in what I say to you, which is that I marry you to my younger daughter, who is no full sister to those two and is a virgin. I will take no dowry from you; I will settle an allowance on the two of you from my own means, and you will stay with me in the place of a son.'
sentences.n: uzawwijuka ibnatī is 'I marry you to my daughter', with both persons as direct objects. shaqīqa, 'full sister', means a sister by both parents; the youngest is only a half sister to the other two. wa-lam ākhudh keeps the madda the print gives the first word. mahr is the bride-price paid by the groom, which he waives. The lord's speech closes here.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ كُنَّا حَتَّى نَصِلَ إِلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu naʿam wa-min ayna kunnā ḥattā naṣila ilā dhālika
sentences.l: So I said, 'Yes — and from-where were we, that we should arrive at that?'
sentences.i: I said, 'Yes; but who are we, that we should attain to that?'
sentences.n: min ayna kunnā is a courteous deprecation: 'where are we from, what are we, that we should reach this?'

sentences.t: فَأَرْسَلَ فِى الْحَالِ لِلْقَاضِي وَالشُّهُودِ وَكَتَبَ كِتَابِي وَدَخَلْتُ بِهَا وَأَخَذَلِي مِنْ كَبِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-arsala fī al-ḥāli li-al-qāḍī wa-al-shuhūdi wa-kataba kitābī wa-dakhaltu bihā wa-akhadhalī min kabīri
sentences.l: So he sent at-once for the judge and the witnesses, and he wrote my contract, and I went-in with her, and he took for me from the chief-of
sentences.i: He sent at once for the judge and the witnesses, and had my marriage contract written, and I went in to her; and he took for me from the chief of
sentences.n: The sentence is cut here at the edge of the section; the chief of the market, presumably, is the one from whom the lord exacted the price of the hand, and the next unit continues. kitāb is a deed, here the marriage contract; dakhala bi-hā, 'to go in with her', is the idiom for consummating the marriage. wa-akhadhalī is printed as one word, wa-akhadha lī, 'and he took for me'.

sentences.t: السُّوقِ مَا لًا كَثِيرًا وَصِرْتُ عِنْدَهُ فِي أَعَزِّ مَكَانٍ
sentences.tr: al-sūqi mā lan kathīran wa-ṣirtu ʿindahu fī aʿazzi makānin
sentences.l: the-market, wealth much, and I-became with-him in most-dear place
sentences.i: the market, and gained much wealth, and I came to hold with him the most honoured station
sentences.n: The sentence begins before this section, so whatever governs al-sūq is out of sight; the genitive is a guess. 'Mā lan' is one word, mālan 'wealth', printed split in two.

sentences.t: وَفِي هَذَا الْعَامِ مَاتَ وَالِدِي فَأَرْسَلَ الصَّاحِبُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ بَرِيدًا وَأَتَانِي بِمَالِي الَّذِي خَلَّفَهُ وَالِدِي
sentences.tr: wa-fī hādhā al-ʿāmi māta wālidī fa-arsala al-ṣāḥibu min ʿindihi barīdan wa-atānī bi-mālī alladhī khallafahu wālidī
sentences.l: And in this the-year died my-father, so sent the-companion from with-him a-courier, and he-brought-me with-my-wealth which left-behind-it my-father
sentences.i: And in that same year my father died, so my father's friend sent a courier from his own side, and he brought me the wealth my father had left behind

sentences.t: وَأَنَا الْيَوْمَ فِى أَرْغَدِ عَيْشٍ
sentences.tr: wa-anā al-yawma fī arghadi ʿayshin
sentences.l: and I the-day in most-comfortable life
sentences.i: and today I live in the most abundant ease

sentences.t: فَهَذَا سَبَبُ قَطْعِ يَدِي الْيَمِينِ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā sababu qaṭʿi yadī al-yamīni
sentences.l: so this cause-of cutting-of my-hand the-right
sentences.i: And this is the reason my right hand was cut off

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبْتُ مِنْهُ وَأَقَمْتُ عِنْدَهُ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَأَعْطَانِي مَالًا كَثِيرًا وَسَافَرْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ فَوَصَلْتُ إِلَى بَلَدِكُمْ هَذَا فَطَابَتْ لِي الْمَعِيشَةُ وَجَرَى لِي مَعَ الْأَحْدَبِ مَا جَرَى
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjabtu minhu wa-aqamtu ʿindahu thalāthata ayyāmin wa-aʿṭānī mālan kathīran wa-sāfartu min ʿindihi fa-waṣaltu ilā baladikum hādhā fa-ṭābat lī al-maʿīshatu wa-jarā lī maʿa al-aḥdabi mā jarā
sentences.l: So I-marvelled at-him, and I-stayed with-him three days, and he-gave-me wealth much, and I-travelled from with-him, so I-arrived to your-town this, so became-good for-me the-livelihood, and happened to-me with the-hunchback what happened
sentences.i: I marvelled at him, and stayed with him three days, and he gave me much wealth. Then I travelled on from him and came to this city of yours, where life grew pleasant for me, and there befell me with the hunchback what befell.
sentences.n: Here the young man's tale ends. The tailor's own story, the one he has promised to tell, begins a few units on.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ مَلِكُ الصِّينِ مَاهَذَا بِأَعْجَبَ مِنْ حَدِيثِ الْأَحْدَبِ وَلَكِنْ لَابُدَّلِي مِنْ شَنْقِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ بَقِيَ الْخَيَّاطُ الَّذِي هُوَ رَأْسُ كُلِّ خَطِيئَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla maliku al-ṣīni mā hādhā bi-aʿjaba min ḥadīthi al-aḥdabi wa-lākin lā budda lī min shanqikum wa-lākin baqiya al-khayyāṭu alladhī huwa raʾsu kulli khaṭīʾatin
sentences.l: So said king-of the-China: This-not with-more-wonderful than tale-of the-hunchback, but there-is-no-escape for-me from hanging-you, but remained the-tailor who he head-of every sin
sentences.i: Then the King of China said: 'This is no more wondrous than the tale of the hunchback, and I must hang every one of you; but the tailor remains, who is the head of every sin.'
sentences.n: After a negative mā, the predicate often takes a redundant bi-: mā hādhā bi-aʿjaba 'this is not more wondrous'. Lā budda lī min is 'I cannot do without' and is printed as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ يَا خَيَّاطُ إِنْ حَدَّثْتَنِي بِشَيٍّ أَعْجَبَ مِنْ حَدِيثِ الْأَحْدَبِ وَهَبْتُكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla yā khayyāṭu in ḥaddathtanī bi-shayyin aʿjaba min ḥadīthi al-aḥdabi wa-habtukum dhunūbakum
sentences.l: Then he-said: O tailor, if you-told-me of-a-thing more-wonderful than tale-of the-hunchback, I-granted-you your-sins
sentences.i: Then he said: 'Tailor, if you tell me something more wondrous than the tale of the hunchback, I will pardon you all your sins.'
sentences.n: The perfect wa-habtukum in the answer to a condition is a promise treated as already done. Shayy is the printed شي (for shayʾ, 'thing'), pointed as the text spells it.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَقَدَّمَ الْخَيَّاطُ وَقَالَ اِعْلَمْ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ أَنَّ أَعْجَبَ مَاجَرَى لِي وَاتَّفَقَ لِى بِالْأَمْسِ أَنَا كُنْتُ قَبْلَ أَنْ أَجْتَمِعَ بِالْأَحْدَبِ أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ فِي وَلِيمَةٍ لِبَعْضِ أَصْحَابِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqaddama al-khayyāṭu wa-qāla iʿlam yā malika al-zamāni anna aʿjaba mā jarā lī wa-ittafaqa lī bi-al-amsi anā kuntu qabla an ajtamiʿa bi-al-aḥdabi awwala al-nahāri fī walīmatin li-baʿḍi aṣḥābī
sentences.l: So at that advanced the-tailor and said: Know, O king-of the-time, that most-wonderful-of what happened to-me and befell to-me yesterday: I, I-was before that I-meet with-the-hunchback, first-of the-day, at a-banquet of-some-of my-companions
sentences.i: Thereupon the tailor came forward and said: Know, O king of the age, that the most wondrous thing that happened to me, and befell me, was yesterday: I was, before I met the hunchback, early in the day, at a feast given by some of my friends
sentences.n: After anna the tailor repeats the subject with a pronoun (anna ... anā kuntu): a loose, Middle Arabic way of building a long sentence. The 'most wondrous thing' is left hanging and resolved by the story that follows.

sentences.t: وَجَمَعَ عِنْدَهُ نَحْوَ عِشْرِينَ نَفَرًا مِنْ أَهْلِ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَفِينَا أَصْحَابُ صَنَايِعَ خَيَّاطِينَ وَقَزَّازِينَ وَنَجَّارِينَ وَغَيْرَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-jamaʿa ʿindahu naḥwa ʿishrīna nafaran min ahli hādhihi al-madīnati wa-fīnā aṣḥābu ṣanāyiʿa khayyāṭīna wa-qazzāzīna wa-najjārīna wa-ghayra dhālika
sentences.l: and he-gathered with-him about twenty persons from people-of this the-city, and among-us possessors-of crafts: tailors and silk-dealers and carpenters and other-than that
sentences.i: and he had gathered at his house some twenty men of this city, and among us were men of various crafts, tailors, silk-merchants, carpenters and the like
sentences.n: The trades are printed with the ending -īn although they stand in apposition to a nominative; read the -īn as the one fixed plural ending of the spoken language.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ مُدَّلَنَا الطَّعَامُ لِنَأْكُلَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭalaʿati al-shamsu mudda lanā al-ṭaʿāmu li-naʾkula
sentences.l: So when rose the-sun, was-spread for-us the-food, that-we-eat
sentences.i: When the sun had risen, the food was spread before us, that we might eat

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِصَاحِبِ الدَّارِ قَدْ دَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا وَمَعَهُ شَابٌّ غَرِيبٌ مَلِيحٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-ṣāḥibi al-dāri qad dakhala ʿalaynā wa-maʿahu shābbun gharībun malīḥun min ahli baghdāda
sentences.l: and behold with-owner-of the-house, he-had entered upon-us, and with-him a-youth, stranger, handsome, from people-of Baghdad
sentences.i: and behold, the master of the house came in upon us, and with him a handsome young stranger from Baghdad
sentences.n: After idhā of surprise the bi- only marks what appears: 'and behold, the master of the house'.

sentences.t: وَعَلَى ذَلِكَ الشَّابِّ أَحْسَنُ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ الثِّيَابِ وَالْجَمَالِ غَيْرَأَنَّهُ أَعْرَجُ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿalā dhālika al-shābbi aḥsanu mā yakūnu mina al-thiyābi wa-al-jamāli ghayra annahu aʿraju
sentences.l: and upon that the-youth best-of what it-is of the-garments and the-beauty, other-than-that-he lame
sentences.i: and that young man wore the finest that clothes can be, and had the finest beauty, except that he was lame
sentences.n: Ghayra annahu is printed as one word, ghayra-annahu, 'except that he'. Aḥsanu mā yakūnu is 'the best that can be', an elative with a relative clause.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا وَسَلَّمَ فَقُمْنَا لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿalaynā wa-sallama fa-qumnā lahu
sentences.l: So he-entered upon-us and greeted, so we-stood for-him
sentences.i: He came in to us and gave greeting, and we rose for him

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ يَجْلِسُ فَرَأَى فِينَا إِنْسَانًا مُزَيِّنًا فَامْتَنَعَ مِنَ الْجُلُوسِ وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ مِنْ عِنْدِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa yajlisu fa-raʾā fīnā insānan muzayyinan fa-imtanaʿa mina al-julūsi wa-arāda an yakhruja min ʿindinā
sentences.l: So he-came he-sits, so he-saw among-us a-person, a-barber, so he-refrained from the-sitting and he-wanted that he-go-out from with-us
sentences.i: He came to sit, but he saw among us a man, a barber, and he refused to sit, and wished to leave our company
sentences.n: Muzayyin, literally 'one who makes comely', is the barber; the word is a plain noun here, not an adjective.

sentences.t: فَمَسَكْنَاهُ وَمَسَكَ فِيهِ صَاحِبُ الْمَنْزِلِ وَحَلَفَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ مَا سَبَبُ دُخُولِكَ وَخُرُوجِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-masaknāhu wa-masaka fīhi ṣāḥibu al-manzili wa-ḥalafa ʿalayhi wa-qāla lahu mā sababu dukhūlika wa-khurūjika
sentences.l: So we-held-him, and held in-him owner-of the-dwelling, and swore upon-him, and said to-him: What cause-of your-entering and your-going-out
sentences.i: We caught hold of him, and the master of the house clung to him and adjured him, and said to him: 'What is the reason for your coming in and your going out?'
sentences.n: Masaka is the spoken-language form for Classical amsaka 'to seize'; masaka fīhi is 'he held on to him'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بِاللَّهِ يَا مَوْلَايَ لَاتَتَعَرَّضْ لِي بِشَيٍّ فَإِنَّ سَبَبَ رُجُوعِي هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنُ النَّحْسُ الَّذِي قَاعِدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla bi-al-llāhi yā mawlāya lā tataʿarraḍ lī bi-shayyin fa-inna sababa rujūʿī hādhā al-muzayyinu al-naḥsu alladhī qāʿidun
sentences.l: So he-said: By-God, O my-master, do-not you-expose for-me with-a-thing, for cause-of my-returning (is) this the-barber the-ill-omened who sitting
sentences.i: He said: 'By God, my lord, do not press me about anything, for the reason I am turning back is this ill-omened barber who is sitting here.'
sentences.n: The relative clause alladhī qāʿidun has no pronoun for 'is': in spoken Arabic the participle stands alone as the predicate.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ مِنْهُ صَاحِبُ الدَّعْوَةِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ تَعَجَّبَ غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ وَقَالَ كَيْفَ هَذَا الشَّابُّ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ وَتَشَوَّشَ خَاطِرُهُ مِنْ هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa minhu ṣāḥibu al-daʿwati hādhā al-kalāma taʿajjaba ghāyata al-ʿajabi wa-qāla kayfa hādhā al-shābbu min baghdāda wa-tashawwasha khāṭiruhu min hādhā al-muzayyini
sentences.l: So when he-heard from-him owner-of the-invitation this the-speech, he-marvelled extreme-of the-marvel, and said: How (is) this the-youth from Baghdad and was-disturbed his-mind from this the-barber
sentences.i: When the master of the feast heard these words from him, he marvelled exceedingly and said: 'How is it that this young man is from Baghdad, and his mind is so disturbed by this barber?'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرْنَا لَهُ وَقُلْنَا لَهُ اِحْكِ لَنَا مَا سَبَبُ غَيْظِكَ مِنْ هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنِ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓarnā lahu wa-qulnā lahu iḥki lanā mā sababu ghayẓika min hādhā al-muzayyini
sentences.l: Then we-looked at-him and we-said to-him: Relate to-us what cause-of your-rage from this the-barber
sentences.i: Then we looked at him and said to him: 'Tell us the cause of your anger at this barber.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّابُّ يَا جَمَاعَةُ جَرَى لِي مَعَ هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنِ مَجْرًى فِي بَغْدَادَ الَّذِي هُوَ بَلَدِي وَكَانَ هُوَ سَبَبَ عَرَجِي وَكَسْرِ رِجْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shābbu yā jamāʿatu jarā lī maʿa hādhā al-muzayyini majran fī baghdāda alladhī huwa baladī wa-kāna huwa sababa ʿarajī wa-kasri rijlī
sentences.l: So said the-youth: O company, happened to-me with this the-barber a-happening in Baghdad which it (is) my-town, and he-was he cause-of my-lameness and breaking-of my-leg
sentences.i: The young man said: 'Friends, an affair befell me with this barber in Baghdad, which is my native city, and he was the cause of my lameness and of the breaking of my leg.'
sentences.n: Alladhī (masculine) refers back to Baghdad as 'town' (balad). Majran, from jarā, is 'a happening' and echoes the verb before it.

sentences.t: وَحَلَفْتُ أَنِّي مَا بَقِيتُ أُجَالِسُهُ فِي مَكَانٍ وَلَا فِي بَلَدٍ هُوَ قَاطِنٌ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ḥalaftu annī mā baqītu ujālisuhu fī makānin wa-lā fī baladin huwa qāṭinun fīhā
sentences.l: and I-swore that-I not I-remained I-sit-with-him in a-place nor in a-town he (is) dwelling in-it
sentences.i: and I swore that I would never again sit with him in any place, nor in any city where he dwelt
sentences.n: Mā baqītu with a following present verb means 'I shall no longer ...'. Fīhā is feminine though balad is masculine; the text is not consistent about the gender of 'town'.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ سَافَرْتُ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ وَرَحَلْتُ مِنْهَا وَسَكَنْتُ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَأَنَا اللَّيْلَةَ لَا أَبَاتُ إِلَّا مُسَافِرًا
sentences.tr: wa-qad sāfartu min baghdāda wa-raḥaltu minhā wa-sakantu fī hādhihi al-madīnati wa-anā al-laylata lā abātu illā musāfiran
sentences.l: and indeed I-travelled from Baghdad and I-departed from-it and I-settled in this the-city, and I the-night not I-spend-the-night except travelling
sentences.i: So I travelled from Baghdad, and left it, and settled in this city; and tonight I will not stay except as a traveller on the road
sentences.n: Abātu is the printed form, as if from bāta yabātu; Classical has abītu 'I spend the night'. I keep the vowel the spelling shows.

sentences.t: فَقُلْنَا لَهُ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ اِحْكِ لَنَا حِكَايَتَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qulnā lahu bi-al-llāhi ʿalayka iḥki lanā ḥikāyataka
sentences.l: So we-said to-him: By-God upon-you, relate to-us your-tale
sentences.i: So we said to him: 'By God, we beg you, tell us your story.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّابُّ وَقَدِ اصْفَرَّ لَوْنُ الْمُزَيِّنِ يَا جَمَاعَةُ اِعْلَمُوا أَنَّ وَالِدِي كَانَ مِنْ أَكَابِرِ تُجَّارِ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shābbu wa-qadi iṣfarra lawnu al-muzayyini yā jamāʿatu iʿlamū anna wālidī kāna min akābiri tujjāri baghdāda
sentences.l: So said the-youth, and indeed had-yellowed colour-of the-barber: O company, know that my-father was from greatest-ones-of merchants-of Baghdad
sentences.i: The young man said, while the barber's face went sallow: 'Friends, know that my father was one of the greatest merchants of Baghdad,'
sentences.n: The young man now begins his own tale. Iṣfarra lawnu is 'his colour turned yellow', that is, he went pale.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَرْزُقْهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِوَلَدٍ غَيْرِي
sentences.tr: wa-lam yarzuqhu al-llāhu taʿālā bi-waladin ghayrī
sentences.l: and not provided-him God, exalted, with-a-child other-than-me
sentences.i: and God Most High had granted him no child but me
sentences.n: Razaqa bi- is 'to provide with'. Taʿālā is the pious formula after God's name: 'exalted is He'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā
sentences.l: So when
sentences.n: The sentence is cut here at the edge of the section; it continues in the next slice.

sentences.t: كَبِرْتُ وَبَلَغْتُ مَبْلَغَ الرِّجَالِ تُوُفِّيَ وَالِدِي إلَى رَحْمَهِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: kabirtu wa-balaghtu mablagha al-rijāli tuwuffiya wālidī ilā raḥmahi al-llāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: I grew-up and I reached the reach-of the-men; my-father was-taken-in-death to the-mercy-of God, exalted-is-He.
sentences.i: When I had grown up and come to manhood, my father died and went to the mercy of God Most High.
sentences.n: The final ه of رحمه stands for ة (raḥmat), as the print spells it, so the phrase is the usual 'to the mercy of God'. tuwuffiya is the passive of tawaffā, 'to be taken (by death)'.

sentences.t: وَخَلَّفَ لِي مَالًا وَخَدَمًا وَحَشَمًا فَصِرْتُ أَلْبَسُ مَلِيحًا وَآكُلُ مَلِيحًا وَكَانَ اللَّهُ أَبْغَضَنِي فِي النِّسَاءِ
sentences.tr: wa-khallafa lī mālan wa-khadaman wa-ḥashaman fa-ṣirtu albasu malīḥan wa-ākulu malīḥan wa-kāna al-llāhu abghaḍanī fī al-nisāʾi
sentences.l: And he-left to-me wealth and servants and retinue, so I-became I-wear fine-things and I-eat fine-things; and God had made-me-hate in the-women.
sentences.i: He left me wealth, servants and a retinue, and I took to wearing fine clothes and eating fine food. But God had turned me against women.
sentences.n: Two features to notice. After ṣirtu the verbs come in the bare imperfect (albasu, ākulu), a Middle Arabic way of saying 'I took to wearing'. And kāna with a perfect verb (kāna al-llāhu abghaḍanī) gives the pluperfect, 'God had made me hate'; the print has the causative abghaḍa with fī al-nisāʾ, 'in the matter of women'.

sentences.t: فَفِي يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ أَنَا مَاشِى فِي أَزِقَّةِ بَغْدَادَ وَإذَا بِجَمَاعَةِ النِّسْوَةِ تَعَرَّضْنَ لِي فِي الطَّرِيقِ
sentences.tr: fa-fī yawmin mina al-ayyāmi anā māshī fī aziqqati baghdāda wa-idhā bi-jamāʿati al-niswati taʿarraḍna lī fī al-ṭarīqi
sentences.l: So in a-day from the-days, I walking in the-alleys-of Baghdad, and behold with a-company-of the-women, they-presented-themselves to-me in the-road.
sentences.i: One day, as I was walking through the lanes of Baghdad, a company of women suddenly came across my path in the street.
sentences.n: māshī is the printed ماشى: the participle māshin (walking) spelled with a final ى, which we point as -ī. wa-idhā bi- is the 'behold' formula: the bi- only marks what suddenly appears. The plural taʿarraḍna agrees with the women (niswa), a feminine plural.

sentences.t: فَهَرَبْتُ وَدَخَلْتُ زُقَاقًا لَا يَنْفُذُ وَارْتَكَنْتُ فِي آخِرِهِ عَلَى مَصْطَبَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-harabtu wa-dakhaltu zuqāqan lā yanfudhu wa-irtakantu fī ākhirihi ʿalā maṣṭabatin
sentences.l: So I-fled and I-entered an-alley not it-passes-through, and I-leaned in its-end upon a-bench.
sentences.i: I fled and went into a lane with no way through, and rested on a bench at the far end of it.
sentences.n: zuqāqan lā yanfudhu is a dead-end lane, literally 'an alley that does not go through'.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَقْعُدْ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ وَإذَا بِطَاقَةِ قَصْرِ الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ فُتِحَتْ وَطَلَعَتْ مِنْهَا صَبِيَّةٌ كَالْبَدْرِ فِي تَمَامِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam aqʿud ghayra sāʿatin wa-idhā bi-ṭāqati qaṣri al-makāni alladhī anā fīhi futiḥat wa-ṭalaʿat minhā ṣabiyyatun ka-al-badri fī tamāmihi
sentences.l: So I-did-not sit other-than an-hour, and behold with a-window-of the-mansion-of the-place which I in-it, it-was-opened, and went-out from-it a-girl like-the-full-moon in its-completeness.
sentences.i: I had sat there barely an hour when a window of the mansion in the place where I was opened, and out of it came a girl like the full moon at its fullest.
sentences.n: The word order is loose: bi-ṭāqati qaṣri al-makāni is 'a window of the mansion of the place', and the verb futiḥat (passive, 'was opened') follows only after the relative clause. 'The full moon in its completeness' is the stock image for a beautiful face.

sentences.t: لَمْ أَرَ عُمْرِي مِثْلَهَا وَلَهَا زَرْعٌ تَسْقِيهِ وَهُوَ عَلَى الطَّاقَةِ
sentences.tr: lam ara ʿumrī mithlahā wa-lahā zarʿun tasqīhi wa-huwa ʿalā al-ṭāqati
sentences.l: I-did-not see my-life the-like-of-her, and to-her a-plant she-waters-it, and it upon the-window.
sentences.i: In all my life I had never seen her like. She had a plant that she was watering, and it stood on the window-sill.
sentences.n: ʿumrī is an accusative of time, 'my life long', so 'ever'. zarʿ is properly 'seed, crops'; here it is a plant she tends on the sill.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَتْ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا وَقَفَلَتِ الطَّاقَةَ وَمَضَتْ فَانْطَلَقَتْ فِي قَلْبِي النَّارُ وَاشْتَعَلَ خَاطِرِي بِهَا وَانْقَلَبَتِ الْبَغْضَةُ مَحَبَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-iltafatat yamīnan wa-shimālan wa-qafalati al-ṭāqata wa-maḍat fa-inṭalaqat fī qalbī al-nāru wa-ishtaʿala khāṭirī bihā wa-inqalabati al-baghḍatu maḥabbatan
sentences.l: So she turned right and left, and closed the-window, and went-off; so it-was-loosed in my-heart the-fire, and it-blazed my-mind with-her, and was-turned-over the-hatred into-love.
sentences.i: She glanced to the right and the left, shut the window and went away. Then a fire broke loose in my heart, my mind blazed for her, and my aversion turned to love.
sentences.n: al-baghḍa is the aversion to women mentioned earlier; the sentence says it turned inside out (inqalabat) into maḥabba, 'love'. The verbs are in the rapid fa- chain typical of the Nights.

sentences.t: فَلَا زِلْتُ جَالِسًا إلَى الْمَغْرِبِ وَأَنَا غَائِبٌ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا
sentences.tr: fa-lā ziltu jālisan ilā al-maghribi wa-anā ghāʾibun ʿani al-dunyā
sentences.l: So I-did-not-cease sitting until the-sunset, and I absent from the-world.
sentences.i: And I sat on until sunset, lost to the world.
sentences.n: lā ziltu + accusative is the idiom 'I did not cease (to be) ...', that is, 'I kept on sitting'.

sentences.t: وَإذَا بِقَاضِى الْمَدِينَةِ رَاكِبٍ وَقَدْ أَمَّهُ عَبِيدُو وَرَاءَهُ خَدَمٌ فَنَزَلَ وَدَخَلَ الْبَيْتَ الَّذِى طَلَعَتْ مِنْهُ الصَّبِيَّةُ فَعَرَفْتُ أَنَّهُ أَبُوهَا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-qāḍī al-madīnati rākibin wa-qad ammahu ʿabīdū wa-warāʾahu khadamun fa-nazala wa-dakhala al-bayta alladhī ṭalaʿat minhu al-ṣabiyyatu fa-ʿaraftu annahu abūhā
sentences.l: And behold with the-judge-of the-city riding, and already they-went-before-him his-slaves, and-behind-him servants; so he-dismounted and entered the-house which went-out from-it the-girl, so I-knew that-he her-father.
sentences.i: And there was the city's judge, riding, with his slaves going before him and servants behind. He dismounted and went into the house from which the girl had come out, and so I knew that he was her father.
sentences.n: The clause wa-qad ammahu ʿabīdū warāʾahu khadamun is obscure as printed. The sense seems to be that his slaves went ahead and servants followed; ʿabīdū has a final wāw (for -uhu, 'his'), and a wa- before warāʾahu may have dropped out. Also qāḍī and alladhī are printed with final ى, which we point as -ī.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إنِّي جِئْتُ إلَى مَنْزِلِي وَأَنَا مَكْرُوبٌ وَوَقَعْتُ عَلَي الْفِرَاشِ مَهْمُومًا
sentences.tr: thumma innī jiʾtu ilā manzilī wa-anā makrūbun wa-waqaʿtu ʿalā al-firāshi mahmūman
sentences.l: Then indeed-I, I-came to my-house, and I distressed, and I-fell upon the-bed grief-stricken.
sentences.i: Then I went home, distressed, and threw myself down on my bed in grief.
sentences.n: Here ʿalā is printed with a final ي (علي); the context shows it is the preposition 'on', not 'upon me'.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَلَيَّ جَوَارِي وَقَعَدْنَ حَوْلِى وَلَمْ يَعْرِفْنَ مَا بِي وَأَنَا لَمْ أُبَلِ لَهُمْ خِطَابًا فَبَكَيْنَ عَلَيَّ وَتَأَسَّفْنَ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿalayya jawārī wa-qaʿadna ḥawlī wa-lam yaʿrifna mā bī wa-anā lam ubali lahum khiṭāban fa-bakayna ʿalayya wa-taʾassafna
sentences.l: So there-entered upon-me girls, and they-sat around-me, and they-did-not know what with-me, and I did-not heed to-them a-speech, so they-wept over-me and they-grieved.
sentences.i: Some of my slave-girls came in to me and sat around me, not knowing what ailed me, and I gave them no word in answer, so they wept over me and grieved.
sentences.n: jawārī may be read 'girls' (jawārin) or 'my girls'. The singular dakhala before a plural subject is normal in Arabic. lam ubali lahum khiṭāban is obscure: it looks like lam ubāli with the long vowel shortened, 'I took no heed, gave no word to them'; I keep the print and translate by the sense.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَتْ عَلَيَّ عَجُوزٌ فَرَأَتْنِي فَمَا خَفِيَ عَلَيْهَا حَالِي فَقَعَدَتْ عِنْدَ رَأْسِي وَلَاطَفَتْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalat ʿalayya ʿajūzun fa-raʾatnī fa-mā khafiya ʿalayhā ḥālī fa-qaʿadat ʿinda raʾsī wa-lāṭafatnī
sentences.l: So there-entered upon-me an-old-woman, and she-saw-me, and not was-hidden from-her my-state; so she-sat at my-head, and she-was-gentle-with-me.
sentences.i: Then an old woman came in to me and saw me, and my condition was not hidden from her. She sat down at my head and spoke kindly to me.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ يَا وَلَدِي قُلْ لِي خَبَرَكَ وَأَنَا أَكُونُ سَبَبَ وَصْلَتِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat yā waladī qul lī khabaraka wa-anā akūnu sababa waṣlatika
sentences.l: And she said: O my-son, say to-me your-news, and I I-will-be cause-of your-joining.
sentences.i: And she said: My son, tell me what has befallen you, and I will be the means of your union with her.
sentences.n: waṣla is 'joining, union', the lover's word for meeting the beloved; the old woman has guessed that the trouble is love. The 'with her' of the idiomatic layer is understood.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا حِكَايَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā ḥikāyatī
sentences.l: So I-said to-her my-story.
sentences.i: So I told her my story.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا وَلَدِي هَذِهِ بِنْتُ قَاضِي بَغْدَادَ وَعَلَيْهَا الْحَجْرُ وَالْمَوْضِعُ الَّذِي رَأَيْتَهَا فِيهِ طَبَقَتُهَا وَأَبُوهَا لَهُ قَاعَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ أَسْفَلَ وَهِيَ جَالِسَةٌ وَحْدَهَا وَأَنَا كَثِيرَمَا أَدْخُلُ لَهُمْ وَلَكِنْ لَمْ تَعْرِفْ وَمَالَهَا إلَّامِنِّي فَشُدَّ حَيْلَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā waladī hādhihi bintu qāḍī baghdāda wa-ʿalayhā al-ḥajru wa-al-mawḍiʿu alladhī raʾaytahā fīhi ṭabaqatuhā wa-abūhā lahu qāʿatun kabīratun asfala wa-hiya jālisatun waḥdahā wa-anā kathīramā adkhulu lahum wa-lākin lam taʿrif wa-mālahā illāminnī fa-shudda ḥaylaka
sentences.l: So she said: O my-son, this one daughter-of judge-of Baghdad, and upon-her the-restraint; and the-place which you-saw-her in-it her-upper-room; and her-father, to-him a-hall large below, and she sitting alone-her; and I often I-enter to-them, but she-did-not know, and not-to-her except-from-me; so tighten your-strength.
sentences.i: She said: My son, this is the daughter of the judge of Baghdad, and she is kept under restraint. The place where you saw her is her upper room, and her father has a large hall below, where she sits alone. I often go in to them, but she has not known [of you], and she has no one but me. So brace yourself.
sentences.n: al-ḥajr is restraint or confinement: the girl is kept in. The clause wa-lākin lam taʿrif wa-mālahā illāminnī is obscure as printed; I read it as 'but she does not know (of you), and she has none but me', and kathīramā and illāminnī are each printed as one word. ḥayl here is 'strength, resolve'.

sentences.t: فَشَدَدْتُ نَفْسِي لَمَّا سَمِعْتُ حَدِيثَهَا وَفَرِحُوا أَهْلِي فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَأَصْبَحْتُ طَيِّبًا
sentences.tr: fa-shadadtu nafsī lammā samiʿtu ḥadīthahā wa-fariḥū ahlī fī dhālika al-yawmi wa-aṣbaḥtu ṭayyiban
sentences.l: So I-tightened my-self when I-heard her-talk, and they-rejoiced my-family on that the-day, and I-became well.
sentences.i: So I braced myself when I heard what she said, and my family rejoiced that day, and I grew well.
sentences.n: fariḥū ahlī puts a plural verb before its subject, a common Middle Arabic habit, here 'they rejoiced, my family'.

sentences.t: فَمَضَتِ الْعَجُوزُ وَرَجَعَتْ وَوَجْهُهَا مُنْغَيِّرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-maḍati al-ʿajūzu wa-rajaʿat wa-wajhuhā munghayyirun
sentences.l: So the-old-woman went-off and returned, and her-face altered.
sentences.i: Then the old woman went off and came back with her face changed.
sentences.n: munghayyir is the printed منغير. I read it as a Middle Arabic passive-reflexive of ghayyara, 'changed' (the Classical would be mutaghayyir); it could also be min ghayr, 'other than (before)'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا وَلَدِي لَا تَسْأَلْ مَا جَرَى لِي مِنْهَا لَمَّا قُلْتُ لَهَا ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā waladī lā tasʾal mā jarā lī minhā lammā qultu lahā dhālika
sentences.l: So she said: O my-son, do-not ask what happened to-me from-her when I-said to-her that.
sentences.i: She said: My son, do not ask what I went through at her hands when I told her that.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِي إنْ لَمْ تَسْكُتِي يَا عَجُوزَ النَّحْسِ عَنْ هَذَا الْكَلَامِ لَأَ فْعَلَنَّ بِكِ مَا تَسْتَحِقِّينَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lī in lam taskutī yā ʿajūza al-naḥsi ʿan hādhā al-kalāmi la-a fʿalanna biki mā tastaḥiqqīna
sentences.l: And she said to-me: If you-do-not become-silent, O old-woman-of the-ill-luck, about this the-talk, I-will-surely-do to-you what you-deserve.
sentences.i: And she said to me: If you do not hold your tongue about this matter, you ill-omened old woman, I will do to you what you deserve.
sentences.n: The oath la-afʿalanna is printed as two words, لا فعلن, with the alif of afʿalanna sitting at the end of the first; read them together. She is reported speaking to the old woman, hence the feminine -ī and -īna.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ لَابُدَّأَنْ أَرْجِعَ لَهَا ثَانِيَ مَرَّةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin lābuddan arjiʿa lahā thāniya marratin
sentences.l: But no-escape that I-return to-her a-second time.
sentences.i: But I must go back to her a second time.
sentences.n: lābuddan is printed as one word, for lā budda an, 'it cannot be avoided that'. Whose words these are is not wholly clear; I take them as the old woman's own resolve to go again to the girl.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ ذَلِكَ مِنْهَا ازْدَدْتُ مَرَضًا عَلَى مَرَضِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu dhālika minhā izdadtu maraḍan ʿalā maraḍī
sentences.l: So when I-heard that from-her, I-increased in-sickness upon my-sickness.
sentences.i: When I heard that from her, my illness grew worse than before.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ بَعْدَ أَيَّامٍ أَتَتِ الْعَجُوزُ وَقَالَتْ يَا وَلَدِي أُرِيدُ مِنْكَ الْبِشَارَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna baʿda ayyāmin atati al-ʿajūzu wa-qālat yā waladī urīdu minka al-bishārata
sentences.l: So when it-was after days, the-old-woman came, and she-said: O my-son, I-want from-you the-glad-tidings.
sentences.i: And some days later the old woman came and said: My son, I want from you the reward for good news.
sentences.n: al-bishāra is both 'glad tidings' and the gift owed to the bringer of them.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ ذَلِكَ مِنْهَا رُدَّتْ رُوحِي وَقُلْتُ لَهَا لَكِ كُلُّ خَيْرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu dhālika minhā ruddat rūḥī wa-qultu lahā laki kullu khayrin
sentences.l: So when I-heard that from-her, was-returned my-spirit, and I-said to-her: to-you all good.
sentences.i: When I heard that from her, my spirit came back to me, and I said to her: You shall have every good thing.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَمَّا كَانَ أَمْسِ مَضَيْتُ إلَى الصَّبِيَّةِ فَنَظَرَتْنِي وَأَنَا مُنْكَسِرَةُ الْخَاطِرِ بَاكِيَةُ الْعَيْنِ فَقَالَتْ يَا خَالَتِي مَالِي أَرَاكِ ضَيِّقَةَ الصَّدْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lammā kāna amsi maḍaytu ilā al-ṣabiyyati fa-naẓaratnī wa-anā munkasiratu al-khāṭiri bākiyatu al-ʿayni fa-qālat yā khālatī mālī arāki ḍayyiqata al-ṣadri
sentences.l: So she said: When it-was yesterday I-went to the-girl, and she-looked-at-me, and I broken-of the-heart, weeping-of the-eye; so she-said: O my-aunt, what to-me I-see-you narrow-of the-chest?
sentences.i: She said: Yesterday I went to the girl, and she looked at me while I was heartbroken and tearful, and she said: Aunt, why do I see you so heavy of heart?
sentences.n: The old woman is now the speaker. munkasiratu al-khāṭiri and bākiyatu al-ʿayni are feminine participles with a genitive of respect ('broken as to the heart'). yā khālatī, 'my maternal aunt', is a polite address to an older woman, and ḍayyiqata al-ṣadri, 'narrow of chest', means distressed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَالَتْ لِي ذَلِكَ بَكَيْتُ وَقُلْتُ لَهَا يَاسِتِّي أَتَيْتُكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qālat lī dhālika bakaytu wa-qultu lahā yāsittī atītuki
sentences.l: So when she-said to-me that, I-wept, and I-said to-her: O-my-lady, I-came-to-you.
sentences.i: When she said that to me, I wept and said to her: My lady, I have come to you ...
sentences.n: The sentence is cut here at the edge of the section; it continues in the next unit. yāsittī is printed as one word, 'O my lady'.

sentences.t: مِنْ عِنْدِ فَتًى يَهْوَاكِ وَهُوَ مُشْرِفٌ عَلَى الْمَوْتِ مِنْ أَجْلِكِ
sentences.tr: min ʿindi fatan yahwāki wa-huwa mushrifun ʿalā al-mawti min ajliki
sentences.l: from [the side of] a youth loving-you, and he overlooking upon the death, from your cause
sentences.i: from a young man who loves you, and who stands on the brink of death for your sake
sentences.n: This sentence began just before the slice: the old woman is telling the girl why she has come. The endings -ki on yahwāki and ajliki are feminine, since she is addressing the girl.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَتَدْرُقُ قَلْبُهَا وَمِنْ أَيْنَ يَكُونُ هَذَا الْفَتَى الَّذِي ذَكَرْتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat wa-tadruqu qalbuhā wa-min ayna yakūnu hādhā al-fatā alladhī dhakartihi
sentences.l: So she said, and [tadruqu] her-heart: And from where is this youth who you-mentioned-him?
sentences.i: Then she said, her heart stirring: 'And where does this young man you speak of come from?'
sentences.n: wa-tadruqu qalbuhā is obscure. I cannot place tadruqu as a verb; the sense wants something like her heart 'softens' or 'throbs' (perhaps a slip for tarruqu or tadiqqu), so the vocalisation is a guess and the print is kept. The girl speaks to the old woman, hence dhakartihi with a feminine -ti.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ هُوَ وَلَدِي وَثَمَرَةُ فُؤَادِي وَرَآكِ فِى الطَّاقَةِ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ مَضَتْ وَأَنْتِ تَسْقِي زَرْعَكِ وَرَأَى وَجْهَكِ فَهَامَ بِكِ عِشْقًا
sentences.tr: qultu huwa waladī wa-thamaratu fuʾādī wa-raʾāki fī al-ṭāqati min ayyāmin maḍat wa-anti tasqī zarʿaki wa-raʾā wajhaki fa-hāma biki ʿishqan
sentences.l: I said: He [is] my-son and the-fruit of-my-heart, and he-saw-you in the window from days [that] passed, and you watering your-crops, and he-saw your-face, so he-went-distracted with-you in-love
sentences.i: I said: 'He is my son, the fruit of my heart. He saw you at the window some days ago while you were watering your plants, and he saw your face, and fell madly in love with you.'
sentences.n: The old woman speaks, and the two -ī endings (waladī, fuʾādī) make a small rhyme. 'Water your crops' is the plants she tends at the window.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَوَّلَ مَرَّةً أَعْلَمْتُهُ بِمَا جَرَى لِي مَعَكِ فَزَادَ مَرَضُهُ وَلَزِمَ الْوِسَادَةَ وَمَا هُوَإِلَّا مَيِّتٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā awwala marratan aʿlamtuhu bi-mā jarā lī maʿaki fa-zāda maraḍuhu wa-lazima al-wisādata wa-mā huwa illā mayyitun lā maḥālata
sentences.l: And I, first time, I-informed-him of-what happened to-me with-you, so increased his-illness and he-clung-to the-pillow, and he [is] not but dead, no recourse
sentences.i: And the first time I told him what had passed between you and me, his illness grew worse and he took to his bed, and now he is as good as dead, without fail.
sentences.n: huwa illā is printed as a single word (هوالا). lā maḥālata 'inevitably' qualifies the whole prediction.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَقَدِ اِصْفَرَّ لَوْنُهَا هَذَا كُلُّهُ مِنْ أَجْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat wa-qadi iṣfarra lawnuhā hādhā kulluhu min ajlī
sentences.l: So she said, and already her-colour had-yellowed: This, all-of-it, from my cause
sentences.i: Then she said, her colour gone pale: 'All this is for my sake?'
sentences.n: The print has no question mark; the sense is a startled question.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ أَيْ وَاللَّهِ فَمَاذَاتُرِيدِينَ
sentences.tr: qultu ay wa-al-llāhi fa-mādhā turīdīna
sentences.l: I said: Yes, by-God. So what you-want?
sentences.i: I said: 'Yes, by God. So what do you want?'
sentences.n: fa-mādhā turīdīna is printed as one word. The ending -īna is feminine, so the old woman is asking the girl.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ اِمْضِي إِلَيْهِ وَأَقْرِئِيهِ مِنِّي السَّلَامَ وَقُولِي إِنَّ عِنْدِي أَضْعَافُ مَاعِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: qultu imḍī ilayhi wa-aqriʾīhi minnī al-salāma wa-qūlī inna ʿindī aḍʿāfu mā ʿindahu
sentences.l: I said: Go to-him, and make-him-read from-me the-peace, and say: Indeed with-me [are] manifolds of-what-with-him
sentences.i: I said: 'Go to him, give him my greeting, and tell him that I feel many times what he feels.'
sentences.n: The imperatives imdī, aqriʾīhi, qūlī are all feminine, so the speaker is the girl and this qultu 'I said' is probably a slip for qālat 'she said'; I keep the print. aqriʾ-hu al-salām is the idiom 'convey my greeting to him'. 'What is with me' is the love she bears.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ قَبْلَ الصَّلَوٰةِ يَأْتِي إِلَى الدَّارِفَإِذَا جَاءَ أَنَا أَنْزِلُ وَأَفْتَحُ الْبَابَ وَأُطْلِعُهُ عِنْدِي وَأَجْتَمِعُ وَإِيَّاهُ سَاعَةً وَيَرْجِعُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ أَبِي مِنَ الصَّلَوٰةِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā kāna yawmu al-jumuʿati qabla al-ṣalāti yaʾtī ilā al-dāri fa-idhā jāʾa anā anzilu wa-aftaḥu al-bāba wa-uṭliʿuhu ʿindī wa-ajtamiʿu wa-iyyāhu sāʿatan wa-yarjiʿu qabla an yaʾtiya abī mina al-ṣalāti
sentences.l: So when it is the day of-the-Friday, before the prayer, he-comes to the-house; and-when he-comes, I, I go-down and open the-door and bring-him-up with-me and meet and-him an-hour, and he-returns before that comes my-father from the-prayer
sentences.i: 'When Friday comes, let him come to the house before the prayer. When he arrives I will come down, open the door, bring him up to me and be with him for an hour, and he can leave before my father returns from the prayer.'
sentences.n: The indicatives (yaʾtī, anzilu, aftaḥu) carry the sense of a plan or command. wa-iyyāhu is the 'and with him' of accompaniment. The print runs al-dār and fa-idhā together as one word.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَ الْعَجُوزِ زَالَ مَاكُنْتُ أَجِدُهُ مِنَ الْأَ لَمِ فَطَابَ قَلْبِي وَرَفَعْتُ لَهَا مَا كَانَ عَلَيَّ مِنَ الثِّيَابِ وَانْصَرَفَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāma al-ʿajūzi zāla mā kuntu ajiduhu mina al-a lami fa-ṭāba qalbī wa-rafaʿtu lahā mā kāna ʿalayya mina al-thiyābi wa-inṣarafat
sentences.l: So when I-heard the-words of-the-old-woman, went-away what I-was finding of the-pain, and my-heart became-glad, and I-lifted-off for-her what was on-me of the-garments, and she-went-away
sentences.i: When I heard the old woman's words, the pain I had been feeling left me and my heart was glad. I took off the clothes I was wearing and gave them to her, and she went away.
sentences.n: The narrator is now the young man. Giving one's clothes to the bearer of good news is a traditional reward. The print splits al-alam into الا لم, and the final verb is read 'she went away' since the old woman is the one leaving.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِي طِبْ قَلْبَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lī ṭib qalbaka
sentences.l: And she said to-me: Be-good your-heart
sentences.i: And she said to me: 'Be of good cheer.'
sentences.n: ṭib qalbaka 'be good in heart' is a set phrase of comfort.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَالَمْ يَبْقَ فِيَّ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الْأَ لَمِ وَتَبَاشَرَ أَهْلُ بَيْتِي وَأَصْحَابِي لِعَا فِيَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā lam yabqa fiyya shayʾun mina al-a lami wa-tabāshara ahlu baytī wa-aṣḥābī liʿā fiyatī
sentences.l: So I-said to-her-not remained in-me a-thing of the-pain; and rejoiced the-people of-my-house and my-companions at-my-health
sentences.i: I told her that no trace of the pain remained in me; and my household and my friends rejoiced at my recovery.
sentences.n: lahālam is printed as one word (lahā + lam). The print again splits two words: al-alam as الا لم and li-ʿāfiyatī as لعا فيتي. The singular verb tabāshara precedes its plural subject, as in Classical.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ أَزَلْ كَذَلِكَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ وَإِذَا بِالْعَجُوزِ دَخَلَتْ عَلَيَّ وَسَأَلَتْنِي عَنْ حَالِي فَأَخْبَرْتُهَا أَنِّي بِخَيْرٍ وَعَافِيَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lam azal kadhālika ilā yawmi al-jumuʿati wa-idhā bi-al-ʿajūzi dakhalat ʿalayya wa-saʾalatnī ʿan ḥālī fa-akhbartuhā annī bi-khayrin wa-ʿāfiyatin
sentences.l: And I-did-not cease thus until the-day of-the-Friday, and-behold-with the-old-woman, she-entered upon-me and asked-me about my-state, so I-informed-her that-I [was] in good and health
sentences.i: And I remained so until Friday, and behold, the old woman came in to me and asked after my condition, and I told her I was well and sound.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi- is the 'and behold' of surprise; the bi- only marks what appears.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ لَبِسْتُ ثِيَابِي وَتَعَطَّرْتُ وَبَقِيتُ أَنْتَظِرُ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ إِلَى الصَّلَوٰةِ حَتَّى أَمْضِيَ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma labistu thiyābī wa-taʿaṭṭartu wa-baqītu antaẓiru al-nāsa yadkhulūna ilā al-ṣalāti ḥattā amḍiya ilayhā
sentences.l: Then I-put-on my-clothes and perfumed-myself and remained I-wait the-people entering to the-prayer until I-go to-her
sentences.i: Then I put on my clothes and scented myself, and I kept waiting for the people to go in to the prayer, so that I could go to her.
sentences.n: This sentence runs across the page break (p. 237 to p. 238) without a stop.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ إِنَّ مَعَكَ فِي الْوَقْتِ فُسْحَةً فَلَوْ مَضَيْتَ إِلَى الْحَمَّامِ وَأَزَلْتَ شَعْرَكَ لَاسِيَّمَا مِنْ أَشَدِّ الْمَرَضِ لَكَانَ فِي ذَلِكَ سَلَاحَلَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu inna maʿaka fī al-waqti fusḥatan fa-law maḍayta ilā al-ḥammāmi wa-azalta shaʿraka lā siyyamā min ashaddi al-maraḍi la-kāna fī dhālika salāḥalā
sentences.l: So said the-old-woman: Indeed with-you in the-time [is] a-leeway; so if you-had-gone to the-bath and removed your-hair, especially from the-severest of-the-illness, it-would-be in that [salāḥalā]
sentences.i: The old woman said: 'You have some time to spare. If you went to the bathhouse and shaved your hair, especially after so severe an illness, it would do you good.'
sentences.n: Two things are obscure. salāḥalā is printed as one word and I cannot read it with certainty: it may be a corrupt ṣalāḥan 'a benefit, soundness', so the translation follows the sense. And lā siyyamā min ashaddi al-maraḍi, literally 'especially from the severest of the illness', I take to mean 'especially after (recovering from) a severe illness'. 'Hair' here means the hair of the head.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ هُوَ الصَّوَابُ لِمَنْ أَحْلِقُ رَأْسِي وَأَعُودُ أَدْخُلُ الْحَمَّامَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu huwa al-ṣawābu liman aḥliqu raʾsī wa-aʿūdu adkhulu al-ḥammāma
sentences.l: So I-said: It [is] the-right-thing; for-whom I-shave my-head and return, I-enter the-bath
sentences.i: I said: 'You are right. I will shave my head, and come back and go into the bath.'
sentences.n: li-man is obscure as printed. The sense wants 'so that' or 'then', perhaps for li-an or fa-; I vocalise the letters as they stand. aʿūdu adkhulu 'I come back and enter' strings two verbs without a conjunction.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْتُ خَلْفَ الْمُزَيِّنِ يَحْلِقُ رَأْسِي وَقُلْتُ لِلْغُلَامِ اِمْضِ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَأْتِنِي بِمُزَيِّنٍ يَكُونُ عَاقِلًا وَقَايِلَ الْفُضُولِ لَا يُصَدِّعُ رَأْسِى بِكَثْرَةِ كَلَامِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma arsaltu khalfa al-muzayyini yaḥliqu raʾsī wa-qultu li-al-ghulāmi imḍi ilā al-sūqi wa-ʾtinī bi-muzayyinin yakūnu ʿāqilan wa-qāyila al-fuḍūli lā yuṣaddiʿu raʾsī bi-kathrati kalāmihi
sentences.l: Then I-sent after the-barber, he-shave my-head; and I-said to-the-boy: Go to the-market and bring-me with a-barber, he-is sensible and [qāyil] of-the-meddling, not he-splits my-head by-abundance of-his-talk
sentences.i: Then I sent for a barber to shave my head, and I said to the boy: 'Go to the market and bring me a barber who is sensible, not given to meddling, one who will not split my head with his endless talk.'
sentences.n: qāyil is printed as such; it is very likely a slip for qalīl, 'scant of meddling', and I translate so. The first verb is printed with the precomposed أ in wa-ʾtinī, as in the print. The barber is the story's irony: he will do exactly what is forbidden here.

sentences.t: فَمَضَى الْغُلَامُ وَأَتَى بِهَذَا الشَّيْخِ السُّوؤِ
sentences.tr: fa-maḍā al-ghulāmu wa-atā bi-hādhā al-shaykhi al-sūʾi
sentences.l: So went the-boy and brought this the-old-man the-evil
sentences.i: So the boy went and brought back this wretched old man.
sentences.n: This is the barber who gives the tale its trouble. The young man's verdict, al-shaykh al-sūʾ 'the evil old man', is a narrator's aside looking back on what followed; the print spells sūʾ with a doubled wāw/hamza (السوؤ).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ سَلَّمَ عَلَيَّ فَرَدَدْتُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala sallama ʿalayya fa-radadtu ʿalayhi al-salāma
sentences.l: So when he-entered he-greeted upon-me, so I-returned upon-him the-peace
sentences.i: When he came in he greeted me, and I returned his greeting.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنِّي أَرَاكَ نَاحِلَ الْجِسْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla innī arāka nāḥila al-jismi
sentences.l: So he-said: Indeed-I I-see-you wasted [of] the-body
sentences.i: Then he said: 'I see that your body has grown thin.'

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مَرِيضًا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu innī kuntu marīḍan
sentences.l: So I-said to-him: Indeed-I I-was ill
sentences.i: I said to him: 'I have been ill.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ هَمَّكَ وَغَمَّكَ وَالْبَأْسَ وَالْأَحْزَانَ عَنْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla adhhaba al-llāhu hammaka wa-ghammaka wa-al-baʾsa wa-al-aḥzāna ʿanka
sentences.l: So he-said: Took-away God your-worry and your-grief and the-distress and the-sorrows from-you
sentences.i: Then he said: 'May God take away your worry and your grief, your distress and your sorrows.'
sentences.n: The perfect adhhaba is optative, 'may God remove', a blessing formula.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ تَقَبَّلَ اللَّهُ مِنْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu taqabbala al-llāhu minka
sentences.l: So I-said: Accepted God from-you
sentences.i: I said: 'May God accept it from you.'
sentences.n: taqabbala Allāhu minka is the usual polite reply to a blessing; the perfect is again optative.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَبْشِرْ يَا سَيِّدِي فَقَدْ جَاءَتْكَ الْعَافِيَةُ تُرِيدُ تَقْصِيرَ شَعْرِكَ أَوْ تُخْرِجُ دَمًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla abshir yā sayyidī fa-qad jāʾatka al-ʿāfiyatu turīdu taqṣīra shaʿrika aw tukhriju daman
