sentences.l: So he-said: Rejoice, O my-lord, for indeed came-to-you the-health. You-want shortening of-your-hair or you-draw-out blood?
sentences.i: Then he said: 'Good news, my lord, for health has come to you! Do you want your hair trimmed, or to be bled?'
sentences.n: The question has no particle, only the tone. The barber also lets blood (cupping), hence akhraja daman. tukhriju is indicative after aw, where Classical would use the subjunctive.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ وَرَدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِىَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ مَنْ قَصَّرَ شَعْرَةً يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ صَرَفَ عَنْهُ سَبْعِينَ دَاءً
sentences.tr: fa-innahu warada ʿani ibni ʿAbbāsin raḍiya al-llāhu ʿanhu annahu qāla man qaṣṣara shaʿratan yawma al-jumuʿati ṣarafa ʿanhu sabʿīna dāʾan
sentences.l: For indeed-it it-came-down from the-son of-ʿAbbās, was-pleased God with-him, that-he he-said: Whoever shortened a-hair [on] the-day of-the-Friday, he-turned-away from-him seventy ailments
sentences.i: For it is reported of Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with him, that he said: 'Whoever trims his hair on Friday, God turns seventy ailments away from him.'
sentences.n: Ibn ʿAbbās (d. c. 687) was a Companion of the Prophet, and sayings are often fathered on him. The barber is quoting this as a hadith, and the attribution is not one I can vouch for. shaʿratan is printed with tā marbūṭa, 'a hair'; it may be a slip for shaʿrahu 'his hair'. The subject of ṣarafa, God, is understood.

sentences.t: وَرُوِيَ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا أَنَّهُ قَالَ مَنِ اِحْتَجَمَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ أَمِنَ مِنْ ذَهَابِ الْبَصَرِ وَكَثْرَةِ الْمَرَضِ
sentences.tr: wa-ruwiya ʿanhu ayḍan annahu qāla mani iḥtajama yawma al-jumuʿati amina min dhahābi al-baṣari wa-kathrati al-maraḍi
sentences.l: And it-was-related from-him also that-he he-said: Whoever had-himself-cupped [on] the-day of-the-Friday, he-was-safe from loss of-the-sight and abundance of-the-illness
sentences.i: It is also related of him that he said: 'Whoever has himself cupped on Friday is safe from losing his sight and from much sickness.'

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ دَعْ عَنْكَ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ وَقُمِ السَّاعَةَ اِحْلِقْ لِي رَأْسِي فَإِنِّي رَجُلٌ ضَعِيفٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu daʿ ʿanka hādhā al-kalāma wa-qumi al-sāʿata iḥliq lī raʾsī fa-innī rajulun ḍaʿīfun
sentences.l: So I-said to-him: Leave from-you this the-talk, and get-up the-hour: shave for-me my-head, for indeed-I [am] a-man weak
sentences.i: I said to him: 'Leave off this talk, get up at once and shave my head, for I am a weak man.'
sentences.n: al-sāʿata, 'the hour', is an adverb meaning 'at once'. qum iḥliq strings two imperatives without a conjunction between them.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma
sentences.l: So he-got-up
sentences.i: So he rose
sentences.n: The sentence is cut here at the edge of the section; it continues in the next unit.

sentences.t: وَمَدَّيَدَهُ وَأَخْرَجَ مِنْدِيلًا وَفَتَحَهُ وَإِذَا فِيهِ اِسْطُرْلَابٌ وَهُوَ سَبْعُ صَفَائِحَ مُطَعَّمٌ بِالْفِضَّةِ فَأَخَذَهُ وَمَضَى إِلَى وَسَطِ الدَّارِ وَرَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ إِلَى شُعَاعِ الشَّمْسِ وَنَظَرَ مَلِيًّا وَقَالَ لِي
sentences.tr: wa-madda yadahu wa-akhraja mindīlan wa-fataḥahu wa-idhā fīhi asṭurlābun wa-huwa sabʿu ṣafāʾiḥa muṭaʿʿamun bi-al-fiḍḍati fa-akhadhahu wa-maḍā ilā wasaṭi al-dāri wa-rafaʿa raʾsahu ilā shuʿāʿi al-shamsi wa-naẓara maliyyan wa-qāla lī
sentences.l: And he-stretched his-hand, and brought-out a handkerchief, and opened it, and behold, in it an astrolabe, and it seven plates, inlaid with the silver; so he took it, and went to the middle of the house, and raised his head to the ray of the sun, and looked a long-while, and said to-me:
sentences.i: He stretched out his hand, drew out a handkerchief and opened it, and there inside was an astrolabe of seven plates, inlaid with silver. He took it and went to the middle of the courtyard, raised his head toward the rays of the sun, gazed a long while, and said to me:
sentences.n: The sentence begins before this section. The first word is printed as one with its object, ومديده, and read here as wa-madda yadahu, 'and he stretched his hand'. The astrolabe is called 'seven plates', that is, it carries seven plates, each engraved for a latitude.

sentences.t: اِعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ مَضَى مِنْ يَوْمِنَاهَذَا الَّذِي هُوَ يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ وَهُوَ يَوْمُ جُمُعَةٍ عَاشِرُ صَفَرٍ سَنَةَ ثَلٰثٍ وَخَمْسِينَ وَسِتِّمِائَةٍ مِنَ الْهِجْرَةِ النَّبَوِيَّةِ عَلَى صَاحِبِهَا أَفْضَلُ الصَّلَوٰةِ وَالسَّلَامِ وَسَبْعِ آلَافٍ وَثَلٰثِمِائَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ مِنْ تَارِيخِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِ
sentences.tr: iʿlam annahu maḍā min yawminā hādhā al-ladhī huwa yawmu al-jumuʿati wa-huwa yawmu jumuʿatin ʿāshiru Ṣafarin sanata thalāthin wa-khamsīna wa-sittimiʾatin mina al-hijrati al-nabawiyyati ʿalā ṣāḥibihā afḍalu al-ṣalāti wa-al-salāmi wa-sabʿi ālāfin wa-thalāthimiʾatin wa-ʿishrīna min tārīkhi al-Iskandari
sentences.l: Know that there-passed from our-day this, which is the day of the Friday, and it is the day of Friday, the tenth of Ṣafar, the year of three and fifty and six-hundred, from the Prophetic Hijra, upon its-master the best of the prayer and the peace, and seven thousands and three-hundred and twenty from the era of Alexander,
sentences.i: Know that there has passed of this day of ours, which is Friday, Friday the tenth of Ṣafar in the year six hundred and fifty-three of the Prophet's Hijra, upon its master be the best of blessing and peace, and in the year seven thousand three hundred and twenty by the era of Alexander,
sentences.n: The date formula. The verb maḍā, 'has passed', is left without the amount of time that should follow it; the clause reads as a bare date. 'Seven thousands' keeps the printed masculine-plural-looking noun with sabʿ as written, where Classical would have sabʿat ālāf. The Alexandrian (Seleucid) era is the year count the astrologer uses beside the Hijra.

sentences.t: وَالطَّالِعُ فِي يَوْمِنَا هَذَا عَلَى مَا أَوْجَبَ عِلْمُ الْحِسَابِ مِنَ الْمِرِّيخِ ثَمَانِ دَرَجٍ وَسِتِّ دَقَائِقَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ṭāliʿu fī yawminā hādhā ʿalā mā awjaba ʿilmu al-ḥisābi mina al-Mirrīkhi thamāni darajin wa-sitti daqāʾiqa
sentences.l: And the ascendant in our-day this, according-to what the science of the reckoning has-required, from Mars, eight degrees and six minutes,
sentences.i: And the ascendant on this day of ours, as the science of reckoning requires, stands eight degrees and six minutes from Mars,
sentences.n: Astrological jargon: al-ṭāliʿ is the rising sign, the ascendant. The numerals keep the printed uninflected shape, ثمان درج 'eight degrees' with the counted noun in the genitive singular-plural, which is not Classical.

sentences.t: وَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّهُ قَارَنَهُ عُطَارِدُ وَذَلِكَ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ حَلْقَ الشَّعْرِ طَيِّبٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ittafaqa annahu qāranahu ʿUṭāridu wa-dhālika yadullu ʿalā anna ḥalqa al-shaʿri ṭayyibun
sentences.l: And it-agreed that Mercury conjoined it, and that indicates that the shaving of the hair is good.
sentences.i: And it so happened that Mercury stood in conjunction with it, which shows that shaving the hair is auspicious.

sentences.t: وَدَلَّ عِنْدِي أَنَّكَ تُرِيدُ الِاتِّصَالَ بِشَخْصٍ وَهُوَ مَسْعُودٌ لَكِنْ بَعْدَهُ كَلَامٌ يَقَعُ وَشَيٌّ لَا أَذْكُرُهُ لَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-dalla ʿindī annaka turīdu al-ittiṣāla bi-shakhṣin wa-huwa Masʿūdun lākin baʿdahu kalāmun yaqaʿu wa-shayyun lā adhkuruhu laka
sentences.l: And it-indicated, in my-view, that you want the joining with a person, and he is Masʿūd, but after it talk occurs, and a thing I do-not mention to-you.
sentences.i: And it showed me that you wish to join company with a certain person, namely Masʿūd, but that some talk will follow, and something I shall not tell you.
sentences.n: شي is printed as it was in the previous night and pointed shayy as spelled (for shayʾ, 'thing'). Masʿūd is the name; the barber alludes to the person the youth will meet.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَضْجَرْتَنِي وَصَغَّرْتَ رُوحِي وَقَوَّلْتَ عَلَيَّ بِفَالٍ غَيْرِ مَلِيحٍ وَأَنَا مَا طَلَبْتُكَ إِلَّا لِتَحْلِقَ رَأْسِي فَقُمْ وَاحْلِقْ رَأْسِي وَلَا تُطَوِّلْ مَعِى الْكَلَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu wa-al-llāhi laqad aḍjartanī wa-ṣaghgharta rūḥī wa-qawwalta ʿalayya bi-fālin ghayri malīḥin wa-anā mā ṭalabtuka illā li-taḥliqa raʾsī fa-qum wa-iḥliq raʾsī wa-lā tuṭawwil maʿī al-kalāma
sentences.l: So I-said to-him: By-God, you-have wearied me and made-small my spirit, and you-have-spoken upon me an omen not good; and I, I did-not seek you except to shave my head; so rise and shave my head, and do-not lengthen with-me the talk.
sentences.i: So I said to him: By God, you have wearied me and cast me down, and uttered an ill omen over me! I sent for you only to shave my head. Get up and shave it, and do not drag out the talk with me.
sentences.n: Two things to notice. وقولت is pointed wa-qawwalta, a form II 'you have made words, pronounced'; it may instead be a spelling of qulta, 'you said', with an intrusive wāw. And ما طلبتك إلا ل- 'I did not seek you except to' is the usual way of saying 'I sought you only to'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَوْ عَلِمْتَ بِالَّذِي رَائِحٌ يَجْرِي لَكَ لَمْ تَعْمَلْ فِي هَذَا النَّهَارِ شَيْئًا وَأَنَا أُشِيرُ عَلَيْكَ أَنَّكَ تَعْمَلُ بِالَّذِي أَقُولُ لَكَ عَلَيْهِ فِي حِسَابِ الْكَوَاكِبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-al-llāhi law ʿalimta bi-al-ladhī rāʾiḥun yajrī laka lam taʿmal fī hādhā al-nahāri shayʾan wa-anā ushīru ʿalayka annaka taʿmalu bi-al-ladhī aqūlu laka ʿalayhi fī ḥisābi al-kawākibi
sentences.l: So he said: By-God, if you-knew of that-which [is] going to-happen to-you, you-would-not do in this day a-thing; and I, I advise you that you do according-to that-which I-say to-you upon it in the reckoning of-the-stars.
sentences.i: Then he said: By God, if you knew what is about to happen to you, you would do nothing at all today. I advise you to do as I tell you, according to the reckoning of the stars.
sentences.n: رائح is the colloquial 'going to', a participle of rāḥa used as a future marker, with the verb following it directly (rāʾiḥ yajrī, 'is going to happen'). لم تعمل after law is the negative in the answer clause, where Classical would use lā or lam with law as a past. And أنك تعمل keeps the indicative where Classical would have the subjunctive.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي مَا رَأَيْتُ مُزَيِّنًا لَهُ مَهَارَةٌ فِي عِلْمِ النُّجُومِ سِوَاكَ لَكِنِّى أَدْرِى وَأَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ كَثِيرُ الْخُزَعْبَلَاتِ وَأَنَا مَا دَعَوْتُكَ إِلَّا لِتُزَيِّنَ رَأْسِي فَجِئْتَنِى بِهَذَالْكَلَامِ الْفَاسِدِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu wa-al-llāhi innī mā raʾaytu muzayyinan lahu mahāratun fī ʿilmi al-nujūmi siwāka lākinnī adrī wa-aʿlamu annaka kathīru al-khuzaʿbalāti wa-anā mā daʿawtuka illā li-tuzayyina raʾsī fa-jiʾtanī bi-hādhā al-kalāmi al-fāsidi
sentences.l: So I-said to-him: By-God, I have-not seen a barber to-him a skill in the science of-the-stars other-than-you; but I know and I-am-aware that you [are] much-of the trifles, and I did-not call you except to adorn my head, and you-came-to-me with this the-talk, the corrupt.
sentences.i: So I said to him: By God, I have never seen a barber with such skill in the science of the stars as yours, but I know and am well aware that you are a man of endless nonsense. I called you only to dress my head, and you bring me this foul talk.
sentences.n: مزينا له مهارة is a relative-less description, 'a barber having skill', where the noun clause follows an indefinite noun. The word بهذالكلام is printed as one word (bi-hādhā al-kalām, 'with this talk'). al-khuzaʿbalāt are idle tales and nonsense; the form is a plural of khuzaʿbalah.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمُزَيِّنُ أَتُرِيدُ أَزِيدُ مِنْ هَذَا فَقَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ بِمُزَيِّنٍ مُنَجِّمٍ عَالِمٍ بِصَنْعَةِ الْكِيمِيَاءِ وَالسِّيمِيَاءِ وَالنَّحْوِ الصَّرْفِ وَاللُّغَةِ وَعِلْمِ الْمَعَانِي وَالْبَيَانِ وَعِلْمِ الْمَنْطِقِ وَالْحِسَابِ وَالْهَيْئَةِ وَالْهَنْدَسَةِ وَالْفِقْهِ وَالْحَدِيثِ وَالتَّفْسِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-muzayyinu a-turīdu azīdu min hādhā fa-qad manna al-llāhu ʿalayka bi-muzayyinin munajjimin ʿālimin bi-ṣanʿati al-kīmiyāʾi wa-al-sīmiyāʾi wa-al-naḥwi al-ṣarfi wa-al-lughati wa-ʿilmi al-maʿānī wa-al-bayāni wa-ʿilmi al-manṭiqi wa-al-ḥisābi wa-al-hayʾati wa-al-handasati wa-al-fiqhi wa-al-ḥadīthi wa-al-tafsīri
sentences.l: So the barber said: Do-you-want [that] I-add more than this? For God has-indeed favoured you with a barber, an astrologer, a knower of the craft of-alchemy and of-sīmiyāʾ and of-the-grammar, the pure, and of-language, and of-the-science of-the-meanings and of-the-clarity, and of-the-science of-logic and of-reckoning and of-astronomy and of-geometry and of-jurisprudence and of-tradition and of-commentary.
sentences.i: Then the barber said: Would you have me add to this? God has favoured you with a barber who is an astrologer, learned in the craft of alchemy and of occult science, in pure grammar and in language, in rhetoric, in logic and arithmetic, in astronomy and geometry, in law, in the Traditions and in Qurʾānic commentary.
sentences.n: Here the barber lists his accomplishments. al-sīmiyāʾ is talismanic or occult science; al-maʿānī wa-al-bayān are the two branches of Arabic rhetoric; al-hayʾa is astronomy; and al-ḥadīth is the corpus of the Prophet's Traditions. al-naḥw al-ṣarf is read as 'pure grammar', though it may name syntax (naḥw) and morphology (ṣarf) together. ازيد follows اتريد without an, a Middle Arabic juxtaposition of verbs.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قَرَأْتُ الْكُتُبَ وَدَرَسْتُهَا وَمَارَسْتُ الْأُمُورَ وَعَرَفْتُهَا وَحَفِظْتُ الْعُلُومَ وَأَتْقَنْتُهَا وَعَلِمْتُ الصَّنْعَةَ وَأَحْكَمْتُهَا وَدَبَّرْتُ جَمِيعَ الْأَشْيَاءِ وَرَكَّبْتُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qad qaraʾtu al-kutuba wa-darastuhā wa-mārastu al-umūra wa-ʿaraftuhā wa-ḥafiẓtu al-ʿulūma wa-atqantuhā wa-ʿalimtu al-ṣanʿata wa-aḥkamtuhā wa-dabbartu jamīʿa al-ashyāʾi wa-rakkabtuhā
sentences.l: And I-have read the books and studied-them, and practised the affairs and known-them, and memorised the sciences and mastered-them, and learned the craft and perfected-it, and managed all the things and put-them-together.
sentences.i: I have read the books and studied them; I have practised affairs and understood them; I have committed the sciences to memory and mastered them; I have learned the craft and perfected it; I have managed all things and put them in order.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: every clause ends in -tuhā, and the literal layer keeps the pronoun at the end so the rhyme is visible.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ وَالِدُكَ يُحِبُّنِى لِقِلَّةِ فُضُولِي وَلِهَذَا خِدْمَتِى عَلَيْكَ فَرْضٌ وَأَنَا قَلِيلُ الْفُضُولِ لَاكَمَازَعَمْتَ وَلِأَجْلِ هَذَا أُدْعَى بِالصَّامِتِ الرَّزِينِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna wālidaka yuḥibbunī li-qillati fuḍūlī wa-li-hādhā khidmatī ʿalayka farḍun wa-anā qalīlu al-fuḍūli lā ka-mā zaʿamta wa-li-ajli hādhā udʿā bi-al-ṣāmiti al-razīni
sentences.l: And your-father used-to love me for the fewness of my meddling; and for-this my service upon-you [is] an obligation; and I [am] few-of the meddling, not as you-claimed; and for the sake of this I am-called by the silent, the sedate.
sentences.i: Your father loved me for my freedom from meddling, and so my service to you is a duty. I am sparing of idle curiosity, not as you claimed, and for that reason I am called the Silent, the Sedate.
sentences.n: The text writes لاكمازعمت as one word, read lā ka-mā zaʿamta, 'not as you claimed'. fuḍūl is meddling, the habit of poking into what is not one's business, and is the opposite of what the barber's nickname claims.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ سَبِيلُكَ أَنْ تَحْمَدَ اللَّهَ وَلَا تُخَالِفَنِي فَإِنِّي نَاصِحٌ لَكَ وَشَفْقَانُ عَلَيْكَ وَأَوَدُّأَنْ أَكُونَ فِي خِدْمَتِكَ سَنَةً كَامِلَةً وَتَقُومُ بِحَقِّي وَلَا أُرِيدُ مِنْكَ أُجْرَةً عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna sabīluka an taḥmada al-llāha wa-lā tukhālifanī fa-innī nāṣiḥun laka wa-shafqānu ʿalayka wa-awaddu an akūna fī khidmatika sanatan kāmilatan wa-taqūmu bi-ḥaqqī wa-lā urīdu minka ujratan ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: And your way was that you praise God and not oppose me; for I [am] an adviser to-you and compassionate upon you, and I-would-like to-be in your service a year complete, and you attend to my right, and I do-not want from you a wage for that.
sentences.i: You ought to praise God and not oppose me, for I am your well-wisher and feel pity for you. I would gladly serve you a full year, and you would give me my due; yet I ask no wage of you for it.
sentences.n: واود ان is printed run together and read wa-awaddu an, 'and I would like to'. شفقان 'compassionate' is a colloquial-looking adjective for Classical mushfiq. وتقوم بحقي is ambiguous; it may mean 'and you would acknowledge my due', or it continues the wish under an, so that 'you' would then take the subjunctive taqūma.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ ذَلِكَ مِنْهُ قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّكَ قَاتِلِي لَا مَحَالَةَ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu dhālika minhu qultu lahu innaka qātilī lā maḥālata fī hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: So when I-heard that from him, I-said to-him: Indeed-you [are] my-killer, no escape, in this day.
sentences.i: When I heard that from him, I said to him: You will surely be the death of me today.
sentences.n: qātilī is the active participle with its pronoun, 'my killer', used as a prophecy; lā maḥāla is 'without fail'.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—احِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, so she fell-silent from the talk the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent and left off the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula of the night. The last word is printed الم—اح with a dash standing for a hidden letter; it is the usual al-mubāḥ, 'the permitted', and the pointing keeps the dash as printed.
